body:
The `site` job of `release.yml` run 44976953856 (tag v0.25.0) failed on the site tests (#3271). So `pages` did not deploy, and https://neotech.github.io/Camcraft/ does not show "CamCraft 0.25.0". PR #3274 fixed the tests on `main` (5c8340b81). The tag does not move, so a re-run of the tag run fails again.

Plan (decision recorded on #3271, comment 7073324082):

1. Make a branch `site/v0.25.0`: v0.25.0 plus only the docs and test fixes of PR #3274 that apply to the 0.25.0 tree. No app code and no section for an operation that came after the tag (V-Carve).
2. One workflow PR on `main` adds the input `site_only` to the existing `workflow_dispatch` of `release.yml`. With that input, only `site` and `pages` run, from the dispatched ref. `publish` stays tag-only. No new trigger. The decision file is `docs/decisions/3271-site-redeploy.md`.
3. Owner ask (a settings change): add deployment branch policy `site/*` to environment github-pages (Settings > Environments > github-pages, or `gh api -X POST repos/NeoTech/Camcraft/environments/github-pages/deployment-branch-policies -f name='site/*' -f type=branch`)
4. Dispatch once on `site/v0.25.0`. The work is done when `pages` is green and the site shows "CamCraft 0.25.0".

Fallback: if the policy is not added, the 0.25.0 site content ships with the deploy of v0.26.0, and this issue closes then.

body:

This step is new in this release (PR #2643). Nothing else runs these tests, so they drifted since v0.24.0. A local run with the pinned zola 0.23.6 shows 73 failures and 1 error on v0.25.0. `main` at dfbe0d8a5 fails the same way (74 failures, 1 error). The failures come from the tree, not from the runner.

Causes:

1. 44 icon-position failures (`site/tests/test_guide_icons.py:118`, and `test_guide_refresh.py:50`). Each operation section now starts with the `catalog:examples` block, and the icon comes after it. Cause: b8e217cb8.
2. Missing site icons: `site/static/icons/{op-slot-undercut,tool-t-slot,tool-keyseat,tool-dovetail,tool-lollipop}.png` (`test_guide_icons.py:165`). The app icons exist in `assets/ui/`. Cause: 5452810e5 (#2714).
3. Slot Undercut has no section in the operation reference (`test_operation_reference.py:58`). Cause: 5452810e5.
4. The post manifest property `rotariesBeforeTraverse` has no row in the site post-processor reference (`test_post_processor_reference.py:23`). Cause: 56e81ffc8.
5. The MCP guide lost the fact "no live transport endpoint" (`test_guide_after_1995.py:18`). Cause: 028495f5c.
6. `test_first_continuous_4axis_part` reads `docs/decisions/1904-continuous-4axis-walkthrough.md`, but the cut moves each decision file into `RECOMMENDED.md`. The test must not read a file under `docs/decisions/`.
7. 18 UI label failures (`test_first_4axis_part.py:173` and the continuous twin). The tool Properties no longer draw the labels as plain string literals. Causes: 97f6cb595, 963d7c381.

Expected: the site tests pass on `main`. The fix changes the guide content, the site icons and the tests so that they match the shipped app. It does not weaken a check without a reason in the PR.

The tag v0.25.0 does not move. After the fix, the coordinator decides how the 0.25.0 site is published, and records the decision on this issue.

body:
Found during the cut of v0.25.0 (release PR #3266).

`cut.yml` runs its jobs on `[self-hosted, linux]`. Each Linux post-merge runner matches that label set, so the release gate can land on any of them. Three facts from the cut:

1. Run 44964821090 landed on wopr-2. A post-merge run ran at the same time on wopr, which looks like the same host. The step "Release gate tier" was cancelled after one minute, with no test run.
2. The UI test binaries abort in 0-2 s with `exit -1` on some runners (#3258). Those failures occurred on skull, egg and wopr.
3. From about 00:13Z on 2026-11-22, no Linux runner was online. Run 44965350029 stayed queued, and the release gate ran locally (the fallback of the `release-cut` skill).

What the runners API shows (2026-11-22). It shows no owner of a runner, so this issue names only the labels:

| Runner | Labels |
|---|---|
| cheese, dude, skull, egg, len-pm, wopr-2 | `self-hosted`, `Linux`, `X64`, `camcraft-post-merge` |
| uma | `self-hosted`, `Linux`, `X64`, `uma-linux`, `camcraft-post-merge` |
| wopr | `self-hosted`, `camcraft-post-merge` |
| m3 | `self-hosted`, `macOS`, `ARM64`, `m3-macos`, `camcraft-pr-test` |

Proposed change (a process and workflow change; it needs the maintainer's approval as a `.github` change):

- Add the label `camcraft-cut` to one or more healthy Linux runners. Change `runs-on` of both jobs in `cut.yml` to `[self-hosted, linux, camcraft-cut]`.
- Keep skull and egg out of the Linux post-merge pool until their UI test binaries start (#3258).
- Change the `runners` skill to match.

This is not on the cut list of v0.25.0. It does not block a cut.

title: Wire ISO post: has() accepts text values such as an empty string, true or 0x1A for wire numbers

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:low
labels.description: Mechanical, one file, no new logic (issue-worker-low)

labels.name: P7
labels.description: Owed polish and small fixes

body:
Found in the two safety reads of PR #3263 (comments 7071252890 and 7071263058). This behaviour is older than that PR.

`has()` in `assets/posts/wire-iso.cps` uses the JS `isFinite`, which converts its argument first. A hand-written stream with `PARAM WireU ""` posts `U0.`, `true` posts `U1.`, and `0x1A` posts `U26.`. The app never writes such values. The stream parser turns each real number into a number, so a text value for a wire parameter is always bad.

Expected: for the wire parameters, check `typeof value !== "number" || !isFinite(value)` and refuse the value by name. Add a test for each of the three examples.

Also: a null `WireTaper` on an angle-word machine gives a second message, "an angle-word taper needs one stated angle". Remove that second message when the first refusal already names the cause. The new test of PR #3263 does not cover a bad `WirePlane` or a good section after a refused one. Add those two cases.

body:

1. Start an empty project in the desktop app.
2. Import one part, such as a small STL box.
3. Open **Stock** and select **From model**.

**Expected result.** Apply creates stock from the part shown in Source. The user can accept the displayed selection without changing it first.

### Evidence

A user reported this on macOS with one imported STL. On desktop build `e6e04f5d0`, the source field starts empty. The picker displays the last eligible model as its default. On the same build, passing the model name explicitly to MCP `set_stock` with `from_model` succeeded for that STL. After saving and reopening the project, the setup retained the source name and the stock bounds matched the model bounds. A synthetic part is sufficient for the regression test.

title: ui: an UndercutLift warning can hide a "Do not touch" hit on avoid part 1 (fold key 217)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:low
labels.description: Mechanical, one file, no new logic (issue-worker-low)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Same class as #3040. `fold_warnings_located` (`crates/ui/src/operations.rs`) groups warnings by a numeric key, and a group prints only the line of its first warning. `Warning::AvoidHit { part, .. }` uses `216 + part`, so the range is 216..=220. `Warning::UndercutLift` (Slot Undercut, commit 5452810e5, 2026-11-19) uses **217**, the key of an `AvoidHit` on part 1. When the undercut lift comes first, the blocking "Do not touch" hit on part 1 folds into the advisory as "repeated on N more moves" and is not shown.

#3040 / PR #3062 moves `DrillUndersize` from 216 to 223 and expected `UndercutLift` at 222 (PR #2836's plan). Keys in use on main: 221 is `FirstTraverseLow` and 224 is `FirstTraverseUnderTable`, so 222 is free.

Done means: `UndercutLift` folds under a key outside 216..=220 that no other warning uses (222), and a pinning test folds one `UndercutLift` and one `AvoidHit` on part 1 and asserts both lines are shown, like `a_drill_undersize_never_hides_an_avoid_hit` in #3062.

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Since PR #3185, the post-merge gate runs one independent run for each merge commit. Several gates now run at the same time. Three runs failed with the same signature: a UI test binary stops in 0-2 s with `exit -1`. The log shows no test output, no panic and no assert. Later runs of the same code pass the same step.

| Run | Commit | Runner | Red step | Gate job time (UTC) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 44948384882 | 273642212 | skull | `ui suites: lib` | 20:50-22:15 |
| 44950073227 | 6ffa808ae | egg | `ui suites: trace_parity` | 21:09-22:08 |
| 44955923206 | ced4dc34e | wopr | `ui suites: egui_app` | 22:16-22:38 |

Evidence from the jobs API:
- wopr and wopr-2 look like two runners on one host. The red run on wopr (22:16-22:38) overlapped the run on wopr-2 for a0fe9f1dc (22:07-22:33).
- The host of skull, egg, len-pm, dude and cheese is not known from the API.
- The same steps passed on uma, wopr-2, dude and cheese, and in the later runs on c59aa0730 and a0fe9f1dc.

Hypothesis: two UI test binaries on one host use one shared resource at the same time. Possible resources are the GPU or wgpu adapter, the display session, a fixed port or a shared temp directory.

Candidate fixes:
1. Serialize the UI suites on one host: one concurrency group for each host, or a host lock around the UI suites steps.
2. Find the shared resource and give each run its own copy.

This is not on the cut list of v0.25.0. The release gate runs on `cut.yml`; it uses a re-run of the failed step for this signature.

title: STEP import removes a short edge from a Fusion solid and then refuses the enlarged gap

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: claimed
labels.description: An agent is working on this - see the claim comment

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
### What happens

CamCraft refuses a Fusion STEP model of a heater block. The user reproduced the failure in the desktop app on macOS (v0.24.0, commit `e6e04f5d0`). The MCP tool `import_model` gives the same result. Two AP214 exports and one AP242 export contain the same edge geometry. All three give this diagnostic:

```text
import_model: corrupt STEP: solidcore: import_step produced an invalid result: 1 of 1 solid item(s) refused; first #14 at check: a vertex sits 1.157e-2 mm off its edges (limit 1e-3) - re-export the model, or import an STL
```

The user can view an STL copy. A STEP copy exported from FreeCAD gives the same gap. The original CAD files stay local.

### Where the gap comes from

A diagnostic probe built the same STEP record twice with the pinned Solidcore version (`2016386`). Only the healing setting changed.

| Measurement | Before healing | After normal import healing |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Edges in the solid | 999 | 998 |
| Gap at the start of spline edge `#3375` | 0.006223 mm | 0.011573 mm |
| Largest vertex-to-endpoint gap in the solid | 0.007736 mm | 0.011573 mm |

The file defines edge `#3407` between vertices `#2564` and `#2120`. The vertices are 0.009944 mm apart. Spline edge `#3375` starts at `#2564`. Healing removes `#3407` and redirects `#3375` to `#2120`. Measuring from that vertex to the same spline endpoint reproduces the reported gap. The diagnostic names the solid (`#14`), so the user cannot identify the affected edge.

FreeCAD (Open CASCADE) keeps both vertices and all 999 edges. It reports one valid, closed solid with 345 faces. The file declares 0.010 mm uncertainty.

### Two limits still apply

The largest gap before healing already exceeds CamCraft's fixed 0.001 mm vertex limit. A separate probe passed the reader's record to the machining mesher at the normal 0.005 mm chord target. The mesher refused face 0 with a measured deviation of 0.011141 mm. Increasing the vertex limit alone would still leave a mesh refusal.

### Decision requested

Can the importer preserve an explicit short edge when collapsing it increases the endpoint error on an adjacent edge? If the preserved solid still exceeds machining tolerance, should CamCraft offer a reduced-fidelity view or refuse it with the measured accuracy? Issue #2976 and PR #2994 provide a precedent for reduced fidelity on an edge-to-surface gap. This case concerns a vertex and a curve endpoint.

**Done means:** A synthetic STEP regression fixture covers two distinct vertices joined by a short edge beside a spline. The test checks the edge count and the endpoint error before and after healing. A second test pins the agreed import outcome when the source exceeds machining tolerance. The user can see which check failed and the measured gap. Machining checks continue to use the accuracy the importer achieved.

**Triage.** P3 because direct STEP import fails and an STL copy works for viewing. `effort:high` because the fix changes geometry repair and needs a regression test.

[STEP build and validation](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/e6e04f5d0/crates/kernel/src/solidcore_step.rs#L297-L337) · [Vertex limit and measurement](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/e6e04f5d0/crates/kernel/src/solidcore_import.rs#L106-L157)

body:
Found in the review of PR #3229 (#3206), comment 7068630733.

In the wire-EDM ISO post (`script_wire_iso`), the U word (about line 375) and the taper angle (about line 357) are not checked for a finite value. A non-finite value then posts as `UNaN` or `ANaN` in the program. The X, Y, I and J words go through the checked path.

Wrong posted G-code is P1 in the AGENTS.md table: the post must refuse the program by name, never write a word that no control can read.

Work:
1. Check U, V and the taper angle for a finite value before they are written, as the other words are checked.
2. Refuse the program by name when a value is not finite.
3. Add a pinning test: a non-finite U and a non-finite taper angle are refused, and no NC file is written.

title: Wire ISO post writes whole numbers without a decimal point (X5 reads as 5 um on many controls)

labels.name: bug

body:
`wire-iso.cps` formats coordinates with `fu(v) = trim(toFixed(3))`, so whole values lose the decimal point: `G0 X0 Y0`, `G1 X4.838 Y0`, `U0 V0`.

Evidence: `out/edm-test-square-3pass-wireiso.nc` lines 10, 14 (`G0 X0 Y0`, `G1 X4.838 Y0`).

Done means: wire-iso writes every coordinate, U/V and angle word with a decimal point (`X0.`, `X5.`), pinned by a golden; or a machine/post option forces it and defaults on, with a test for each setting.

body:
`xtask` already discovers directory suites (`tests/<suite>/main.rs`, #927), but three places still assume flat test files or run the whole binary:

- `xtask/src/assets.rs:48` reads only `crates/<d>/tests/{b}.rs`. Folding any post or machine test into a directory suite breaks `#923` asset selection.
- `xtask/src/catalog.rs:146` checks `crates/app/tests/example_catalog.rs` instead of `suites::entry(root, "app", "example_catalog")`.
- `xtask/src/plan.rs:181` (`may_run_ignored`) returns `true` whenever `mod x;` appears in `main.rs`, so every directory suite gets a heavy step even without `#[ignore]` tests.
- `xtask/src/quick.rs:186-195` (`map_modules`) merges Gate maps across all submodules of a directory suite and runs the whole binary (`p.whole`). Editing helper code inside one submodule also runs the whole binary (`quick.rs:103-133`).

Update `assets.rs`, `catalog.rs`, and `plan::may_run_ignored` to walk `suites::sources` / `suites::entry`. Update `quick.rs` to match Gate maps per source file (`suites::Source`) and pass libtest module filters (`--test <suite> <submod>::`) when only specific submodules match or when one submodule changes outside `#[test]` fns. Fall back to the whole binary only when `main.rs` or a shared module changes.

Evidence and measurements: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/919#issuecomment-7065686766

Done means: `xtask` unit tests verify that a directory suite triggers `#923` asset selection, `#2393` catalog selection, accurate `may_run_ignored` detection, and `<submod>::` selection in `quick`.

title: Post-merge gate: one independent run per merge, so a red run names one merge

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
A small, separate slice of the post-merge work. #2908 (lanes, claimed by the maintainer) stays as it is. Proposed in the mkinney comments on #2908 of 2026-11-21.

## What happens now

`post-merge.yml` uses one concurrency group for `main` (`post-merge-main`, `cancel-in-progress: false`). One run at a time; a second push waits, and a third push cancels the waiting one. A merge batch costs cancelled runs, and a red run covers several merges, so finding the breaking merge needs a bisect (#3111 took hours).

## Wanted

1. One concurrency group per commit: `post-merge-${{ inputs.ref || github.sha }}`, `cancel-in-progress: false`. Each push runs on its own free `camcraft-post-merge` runner and always finishes; nothing waits behind another run and nothing is cancelled. The `gate` job does not change. With today's two runners (wopr, uma) two merges are gated at once; more runners only add capacity.
2. Results can now finish out of order. The `report` job gets its own concurrency group (`post-merge-report`, `cancel-in-progress: false`) and a full-history checkout. `.github/scripts/post-merge-report.sh` keeps the last reported commit in a hidden marker in the rolling issue body (`<!-- post-merge-last-sha: <sha> -->`) and skips (notice only) a run whose commit is an ancestor of that sha and not equal to it (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`). No new secrets or repository variables.
3. An xtask test (like `xtask/tests/post_merge_report.rs`) pins: the per-commit group, `cancel-in-progress: false`, and the report skipping an older commit.

This is a workflow change: the maintainer decides (the review labels it `needs-maintainer`).

Done means: two pushes in a row each get a full post-merge run that finishes (neither is cancelled); a red run names exactly its own commit; an older green run never closes the rolling issue that a newer red run opened (pinned by the xtask test).

title: 2D Pocket rest pass drops corner reliefs whose start point is on the rest center boundary

labels.name: bug

labels.name: area:2d

body:
What happens: a 2D Pocket rest pass with a corner relief (#2400) cuts the relief at only some corners. The other corners keep their material. No note or warning tells the user.

Expected: the rest pass cuts a relief at each inside corner that the rest area touches. If it cannot cut one, it says so in a note.

Evidence:
- The pocket is 30 x 30 mm with sharp corners. The rest tool is 6 mm, with `CornerReliefKind::Dogbone`. The entered previous tool is 16 mm.
- `pocket_relief_plan` gives 4 reliefs, with the start points (3,3), (27,3), (3,27) and (27,27).
- `rest_pocket_with_relief` cuts only the relief at (3,3).
- The cause is the filter in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/rest2d.rs` (`rest_pocket_with_relief` on main): `.filter(|r| plan.center.contains(r.start))`. Each start point is on the boundary of `plan.center`. `Region::contains` gives `true` for (3,3) and `false` for the other three.
- The plain pocket (`pocket_entered_with_relief`) cuts all 4 reliefs. The rest pass where the previous tool fits nowhere also cuts all 4.

Found while I merged main into PR #2822 (#2033). The test `crates/motion/tests/rest_relief.rs` on that branch shows the result. It pins that the two rest modes agree, and does not pin the count of 4.

Workaround: use a plain pocket with the relief, not a rest pass.

Done means: a rest pass with a relief cuts each relief whose corner the rest area touches. A test pins all 4 dogbone ends on the fixture above. A relief that the pass cannot cut gives a note.

labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
## What is missing

AGENTS.md has no rule that makes an agent fix its own blocked pull requests before it starts new work. Open PRs with `conflicts` or `needs-rework` wait while agents claim new issues.

## The maintainer's words (2026-11-21)

"Lets add a new law to the AGENTS.md before each new task start. Check Pull requests that is created by current user account - that has label "conflicts, need-rework". And then fix those before picking up any new issue. Make sure this is a docs change that get pushed and merged and signaled over issue 681 as a process change. On the process change dictate that agent files and skills should be reloaded."

## Required change

- Add a new law to AGENTS.md. Name it in bold, as the other rules are named, so that skills and agents can cite it. Suggested name: **Own blocked PRs first**.
- The law: before an agent claims or starts any new issue, it lists the open PRs of the current account that carry `conflicts` or `needs-rework` (`gh pr list --state open --author @me --label conflicts` and `--label needs-rework`; the label is `needs-rework`). The agent fixes each one before it picks a new issue.
  - `conflicts`: merge `origin/main` into the branch (never rebase, never force-push), run the targeted gate, push, as the `resolve-conflicts` skill says.
  - `needs-rework`: fix each review finding on the same branch with a plain push, as "Pull Request Law" says (the PR is a draft first, `needs-rework` is replaced when the review is clean).
  - The existing orders stay first: a `P1` or `P2` PR before other PRs, and the standing order for outside PRs.
- Reconcile the existing text that this law changes. "Refresh only at merge time" says that the author's agents do not touch a conflicting PR. The new law overrides this for the PRs of the current account. Edit that bullet so the two rules do not disagree.
- Add the check as a step to the skills and agents that start work: `work-issue` (step before the claim), `.claude/agents/coordinator.md` (before it dispatches a worker for a new issue), and the `issue-worker-*` agent files if they claim an issue. Keep each edit to a few lines.
- A PR of this change has the line `Process change: yes` in its body. It does not edit `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`.

## Process change notice

The merging session runs `cargo xtask process-bump` after the merge and comments on the pinned issue #681. The comment must say: **agent files and skills must be reloaded** (a running session reloads `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/agents/` and `.claude/skills/`; a fork syncs them as `fork-sync` says). Add this "reload" line to the fixed format of the #681 comment in AGENTS.md, so that each process notice carries it.

## Done means

- The law is in AGENTS.md and the edited bullet does not disagree with it.
- `work-issue`, the coordinator agent and the issue-worker agents carry the check.
- The PR is merged, the process bump PR is merged, and #681 has the comment with the reload instruction.

title: 2D Contour: Lead in/out None still generates a linear lead-in

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
## What happens

A 2D Contour in `O4 Cam Plate master` still shows a linear lead-in when the user sets **Lead in/out** to **None**.

The user also sets these values:

- **Lead out > Type:** None
- **Before lead-in:** 0.0 mm
- **After lead-out:** 0.0 mm
- **Overlap past the start:** 0.0 mm

The user generates the operation again after the changes. The viewport still shows a straight line at the contour entry.

Changing the lead to **Arc** changes the entry shape. Changing it to **Linear** gives the same straight entry. Changing it back to **None** does not remove that entry.

A screenshot from 2026-11-21 shows the operation `2D Contour1`, the selected **None** values, and the remaining straight segment.

## Expected

When the lead-in and lead-out are **None**, the first XY cutting move starts on the contour path. The path has no straight or arc lead segment before that move.

Entry, plunge, retract, rapid, and level-link moves can remain. They must not appear as a lead feed at the contour seam.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a project with a closed 2D Contour operation.
2. Open **Lead in / Lead out**.
3. Set **Lead in/out** to **None**.
4. Set **Lead out > Type** to **None**.
5. Set both extensions and the overlap to 0.0 mm.
6. Click **Generate**.
7. Select the first cutting move near the contour seam.
8. Observe the remaining straight entry segment.
9. Change **Lead in/out** to **Arc**, then to **Linear**, then to **None**.
10. Observe that **Arc** and **Linear** change the shape, but **None** restores the straight entry instead of removing it.

## Related

Issue #3019 covers a generated linear lead that crosses its own ring. The report also says that `lead: "none"` posts. This issue covers a different result: the UI and the posted path still contain an entry lead when the user selects **None**.

## Done means

- A UI or app test changes a Contour from a linear lead to **None**, applies the draft, and generates the operation.
- A test asserts that the first cutting move starts on the contour path with no added lead segment.
- A test covers an explicit **Lead out > None** value with zero extensions and zero overlap.
- The generated path and posted output contain no linear or arc lead when both lead shapes are **None**.
- A regression test proves that **Arc** and **Linear** still generate their selected shapes.

Changelog: A 2D Contour with both lead shapes set to None no longer keeps a linear lead-in in the generated path (#3132).

body:
Found during #3021.

## What happens
PR for #3021 adds closing wall and island rings to the plain 2D Zigzag pocket (`pocket_over_with_relief` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket.rs`). Two other pass plans still cut Zigzag rows with no closing ring:

- `pocket_avoid` (2D pocket with "Do not touch"), `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket_avoid.rs`: each level calls `plan_passes(..., strategy)`, and Zigzag gives rows only.
- The 3D pocket levels that call `plan_passes` with Zigzag or Auto.

The rows touch a wall or an island only at their ends. A cusp stays between each two ends over the full depth (about 0.17 mm on a straight wall with a 6 mm tool and a 2 mm stepover, more on a rounded corner).

## Expected
With stock to leave 0, the Zigzag rows of these plans close with one ring on each boundary loop, as the plain 2D pocket does after #3021. Use `pocket_zigzag::rest_passes` (rows 0.01 mm inside, lattice row points, then the rings).

## Related observation
A 30 x 30 pocket with a 10 x 10 island, an 8 mm tool, a 3 mm stepover and a helix entry gives crossing feed pairs between two helix entries of different passes. The cutter-center band is only 2 mm wide there. The post check blocks the program. This is on upstream/main before #3021 too. The pin `blended_zigzag_turns_do_not_cross_the_closing_rings` uses a plunge entry for this reason.

## Done means
A pin like `crates/motion/tests/pocket_wall_finish.rs` for `pocket_avoid` (and for a 3D pocket level) fails before the change and passes after it. The crossing check stays clean.

body:
Follow-up from the review of PR #3125 (#3084), comment 7060737872.

The posed first-traverse law of PR #3125 reads the work through every pose of the work-turning rotaries. It takes each rotary line through the WCS origin, the same premise as the index-swing clause (`crates/app/src/posting_index_swing.rs` lines 28-40).

A machine file can state a `pivot` or an `offset` for a rotary. No shipped machine file does this, but a user file can. Then the line does not pass through the WCS origin, and the law reads the swept set about the wrong line. The reading can be too low, and the post is not blocked.

Work:
1. When a work-turning rotary states a non-zero `pivot` or `offset`, read the swept set about the stated line, or refuse the operation by name.
2. Apply the same rule to the index-swing clause.
3. Add pinning tests for a machine with an offset rotary line: one refused case and one clear case.

body:
## What is missing

The user documentation has no reference for the post-processor format. A user who writes or changes a `.cps` post cannot find out what the post receives or what it must write. The user must read the source to debug a post.

The facts exist, but only for developers:

- `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` describes how to write a `.cps` post.
- `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md` specifies the record stream and its property table.
- `site/content/guide/check-and-post/posting.md` and `machines.md` describe the workflow, not the format.

## Why

The maintainer asked on 2026-11-21 for this reference, so that people can debug their posts on their own. He set the priority to P3.

## What to add

A reference page in the user guide (`site/content/guide/reference/`), written in plain English. It names these items:

- The manifest properties of a post and what each one does.
- The hooks that the engine calls, in the order of the call, with their arguments.
- The record stream and its properties (from `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md`).
- The functions and values that the prelude gives to a post.
- The refusal messages of the post gate, with the cause and the fix for each.
- How to run a post by itself and see its output, so that a user can find an error.
- One small complete example post, with its output.

Write the page from our own documents and code only. Do not use text from any other product (Clean-Room Protocol). Keep the page in step with the code: a test or a link check must fail when a manifest property in `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` is not in the page.

## Done means

- The page is in the user guide and the site builds with it.
- Each manifest property and each hook is in the page.
- A user can find the cause of a post refusal from the page.
- The page has a pointer from `check-and-post/posting.md`.

Priority note: AGENTS.md reserves `P1`-`P3` for defects. The maintainer named `P3` in his own words, so the label stands.

title: Circular: a helix entry with several rings touches the last ring's helix, and verification blocks it

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found while fixing #2898.

## What happens

A flat Circular with several rings and a helix entry gets blocking `Crossing` warnings. Verification refuses the program. The post is held. The program is refused, not unsafe.

Reproduce with the job of #2898, with entry `Helix` and `helix_radius` 1:

- center [0,0], radius 10, tool EM-0600-4FL (25 mm flutes), stepover 2, stepdown 2
- top Z20, bottom Z0, clearance Z30, stock_to_leave 0

Generation reports pairs such as `feed moves 2 and 84 cross in XY at shared depth`. Each pair is a helix arc of ring k-1 and a helix arc of ring k at the same level.

## Cause

The Circular is ring-major: each ring runs its own level ladder, with its own entry at each level. Each helix passes through its ring's start, and its centre is one helix radius inward. When the stepover is two helix radii, the helix of ring k-1 touches the helix of ring k at the start of ring k. The two helices share one depth band. The crossing law (`crates/sim/src/verify/crossing.rs`) counts a touch as a crossing.

## What was tried

The fix branch of #2898 tried the pocket's z-major order for the flat mode (all rings at one plane). That removed the crossings. But the inner rings then started with an axial plunge that was not named, also under a ramp entry. Four ramp-entry tests went red. The branch dropped that approach (`docs/decisions/2898-circular-ring-links.md`).

## Expected

The helix entry of each later ring is placed so that it does not touch the helix of the ring before it, or the parameters are refused before generation with a named cause.

## Workaround

Use the plunge or the ramp entry, or one ring only.

body:
Follow-up from #3084 (branch `issue/3084-two-rotary-first-traverse`, decision `docs/decisions/3084-posed-first-traverse.md`, "Known limits").

The post sends Z, then X/Y at that height, then the move with the rotary words (`fanuc.cps` `traverseZ`, `xyFirst`, `onRapid`). During the X/Y traverse each rotary that turns the work stands where the previous program left it.

#3084 reads the multi-axis and rotary kinds through every such pose. It does not read these operations:

1. A 3+2 operation (`Tilt`) on a machine with a tilting rotary that turns the work (for example the microARC 4 A, or a trunnion). The #2987 law reads the stock and the fixtures along the plane's tool axis, at the pose of the operation (`first_traverse::judge`, frame branch, `work_tilts`).
2. A cross drill on such a machine.

Risk: the first rapid can go through the stock, the part or a fixture that the previous program left turned up, and no law refuses it.

Work:
1. Read these operations with `verify::first_traverse_low_posed` (the sphere about the WCS origin for two work-turning rotaries, a full turn about the line for one), or refuse them by name.
2. Check the shipped examples on the microARC 4 (`examples/first-4axis-part.camproj` has slot operations, not 3+2) and the index-swing tests before the change. A shipped example that changes needs the maintainer.
3. Add pinning tests: one refused, one clear.

Premise: the unknown start is at the tool-change height (maintainer decision on PR #2997).

title: Proposal: add a Heidenhain Klartext milling post, starting with the iTNC 530

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: needs-research
labels.description: Large idea with open questions: research and file sub-issues before any code

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P8
labels.description: Larger idea needing design or research before code

body:
## What is missing

We want to post a CamCraft milling job as a conversational Heidenhain Klartext (`.H`) program. Our first target is a Fehlmann Picomax 55 with an iTNC 530 running NC software `340490-03`. CamCraft already writes Heidenhain DIN/ISO programs. Issue #3095 tests that post. Issue #2227 proposes a reader for Klartext files. This proposal concerns the writer.

## Proposed design

- Add one **Heidenhain Klartext** post alongside the DIN/ISO post. Keep the implementation, machine data, and test fixtures in CamCraft.
- Let the machine definition identify the installed control, its NC software, and its tool-change procedure. Record installed options when a supported feature needs them.
- Let the post select the documented syntax for that combination. For example, the Picomax needs a manual tool change with the quill at its physical change position. Other iTNC 530 machines can have a different tool changer.
- Start with one metric setup, three linear axes, stock bounds, preset selection, straight moves, plunges, and constant-height XY arcs. Refuse unsupported operations by name. Drilling cycles, tapping, probing, and tilted planes can have separate acceptance criteria later.

## What the local prototype shows

The prototype has one output implementation. It accepts the exact model and release above. Changing only the configured release to `340490-04` or `606425-04` makes it refuse the job before writing a file.

We ran two CamCraft programs on the Heidenhain iTNC 530 programming station, NC software `606425-04 SP20`. Its converter accepted all 41 blocks of a single-tool contour and all 63 blocks of a two-tool program. Test Run reached all three and five programmed stops, respectively. Both runs reached the end of the program without a logged NC error.

This supports those two programs on the station release. Acceptance on the physical `340490-03` installation remains open. Cycle 247 does not activate the preset during Test Run. Preset activation, quill clearance, and physical coolant operation still need checks on the machine. [HEIDENHAIN manuals for NC software 340 49x-03](https://content.heidenhain.de/doku/tnc_guide/html/en/index/1242135142456/1242135142480/1242135142485/1242135142485.html)

## Questions for the maintainers

1. Should the first release require an exact NC software match? When two releases document the same feature, what evidence should let them share the same output?
2. Which facts belong in the existing machine definition, and which should CamCraft maintain for each supported control? Tool-change behavior and supported cycle parameters are the first cases we would use to check that boundary.
3. Would one bounded draft PR suit the project? We propose to rework the local prototype after agreement, then submit the machine definition, post, golden output, and refusal tests together. We can split the machine-data changes first if that is easier to review. We would include the manual references, station results, and outstanding machine checks in the PR.

**Done means:** The maintainers record whether to proceed, the first supported scope, the evidence required, and the preferred PR split. We will wait for that decision before submitting code.

Suggested triage: `enhancement`, `needs-research`, `area:post`, `P8`, `effort:high`, `source:agent`.

title: Mill-turn: no law judges the first traverse of a rotary kind on the spindle C (radial live tool)

labels.name: source:agent

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

body:
Follow-up from #3083.

#3083 brings the mill kinds on a mill-turn under the first-traverse laws of a mill. It does not bring the rotary kinds (`Mode::Rotary`, for example `RotaryContour`) under them on a mill-turn.

On a mill-turn, a rotary kind turns the bar on the spindle C under a radial live tool. The mill premise (an upright tool over an unknown X/Y at the tool-change height) does not apply to that tool. The swept law of #2965 then refuses each such program, for example the shipped C-axis tests (`c_axis_live.rs`, `c_axis_unwind.rs`). So #3083 keeps these kinds out of the law, and decision `docs/decisions/3083-mill-turn-first-traverse.md` records it.

Risk: the first rapid of a radial live-tool rotary operation on a mill-turn can go through the bar, the chuck or the tailstock. No law refuses it. This was also true before #3083.

Work:
1. Judge the first rapid of a rotary kind on a mill-turn from the turret index position, with the live-tool law of #3077 (`verify::live_first_traverse`), after #3077 merges.
2. Add pinning tests: one refused case and one clear case.

Related: #3077, #3083, #2965.

body:

2. A multi-axis kind on a machine whose table tilts: the #2901 tip law reads the part frame. When the table tilts the work, the part frame at the first traverse is the pose that the previous program left, not the pose of the operation.

Work:
1. For each case, read the work through every pose that the previous program can leave (the full range of each rotary that turns the work), or refuse the operation by name.

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Found during the work on PR #2927 and PR #3010 (#2919, #2973).

The STEP reader gives an item that no representation lists (no unit context) the default units: 1 mm per length unit and the radian per angle unit. After PR #2927, a millimetre-only file keeps such items, because the length default is the file's own unit.

The angle default is not checked. A file can state a plane angle unit in degrees in its only context and also hold an item with no context. The reader then reads the angles of that item in radians. The imported geometry is wrong, and the import gives no warning.

`main` has the same gap today. PR #2927 does not make it worse.

Work:
1. Apply the rule of the length unit to the angle unit: keep an item with no context only when every stated angle unit is the default (the radian), or no angle unit is stated.
2. Otherwise, refuse the item by name, as the length-unit refusal does.
3. Add a pinning test: a degree-only file with an unlisted item that uses an angle (a cone or a conical surface).

The heavy lane (release, `--ignored`) is red on `main`. The batch tier does not show it: the test has `#[ignore]` and runs only in the heavy lane and in the gate of a cut. The gate of the next cut will fail on it.

## What fails

`camcraft-app`, test binary `pocket3d_hsm`, test `the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean`.

- On Windows, on `main` at `ee91ac3e5` with no other change, the test gives the counts (3158, 3130, 1141).

- The new counts are equal to the macOS values that the test pins for #2371.

## Evidence

- The second review of PR #2927 (2026-11-20) made the same note for the Linux pin: the pin of this test was stale after PR #2904, and the heavy lane was red with no issue.

## Cause, as far as known

The STEP reader and the machining mesh changed on 2026-11-20 (PR #2904, PR #2934, PR #2994). The mesh of the user's bore model is different, so the adaptive passes have other counts. Not known: which of the three PRs moved the counts, and why the Windows counts are now equal to the macOS counts.

- The cause is named: the commit that moved the counts, and why.
- The test verifies clean, and its pins have the correct counts for each platform, with the reason for each change in a decision file. A pin is not changed only to make the test pass: the work first shows that the new toolpath is correct (the verification of the test stays).
- `cargo xtask gate release --only "app heavy: pocket3d_hsm"` is green on Windows.

Refs #2371, #2904, #2934

body:
## Problem

`fold_warnings_located` in `crates/ui/src/operations.rs` groups the warnings by a key. Two kinds on `main` use the same key:

- `Warning::AvoidHit { part: FixturePart::Shank, .. }` gives `216 + 0 = 216` (the avoid range is `216..=220`).
- `Warning::DrillUndersize { .. }` gives `216`.

A group prints only the line of its first warning. When a program has the two warnings, the pane shows one line. The second finding is not visible. The `AvoidHit` finding is a blocking verdict for a protected "Do not touch" item.

## Fix

Give `DrillUndersize` a free key (for example `223`). Add a pin in `warning_fold_tests` that folds one `DrillUndersize` and one `AvoidHit` shank hit and asserts two lines.

## Context

The clear-out refresh of PR #2836 found the defect. That refresh moved `UndercutLift` from `217` to `222` for the same reason. This issue is for the `DrillUndersize` key on `main` only.

body:
A user who puts `camcraft-cli` on their PATH with a symlink (the usual way on macOS, where the binary is inside `CamCraft.app/Contents/MacOS/`) cannot post. MCP clients (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Cursor) are set up with such a path.

Reproduced on v0.24.0 (macOS, `camcraft-0.24.0-macos-universal.zip`), with one project:

| Started as | `process <project> -o out.nc` |
|---|---|
| `/Applications/CamCraft.app/Contents/MacOS/camcraft-cli` | rc 0, posted |
| a symlink to that file, in another folder | rc 1 |
| a copy of that file, in another folder | rc 1 |

The error of the symlink:

```
ERROR camcraft_app::posting::files: shipped posts file tormach.cps: no posts folder found - the program needs its assets/posts directory beside the executable (looked in: <folder of the symlink>/assets/posts)
camcraft-cli: post: built-in post Tormach PathPilot: no posts folder found ...
```

Cause: the posts folder is found beside the path of the started executable, without resolving the symlink to the real file.

Done means:
- A symlinked `camcraft-cli` finds the shipped posts (resolve the executable path with `std::fs::canonicalize` before the lookup), with a test.
- A plain copy still refuses with a clear message, as now. That message names the setting or environment variable to point at an assets folder, if there is one; otherwise it says to run the binary from the install folder or to use a symlink.

Some halo segments disappear at some angles and zoom levels (see below). | | `main` at acd5b02d3 | Wedge | | `main` + #2989 | Wedge | The pick highlight was rewritten after v0.24.0, in PR #2256 (#2201: cached geometry, one batched mesh of stroke paths). Thus the wedge is a regression of that change. - A probe of `egui::epaint::Tessellator` with a thin, acute closed path does not extend past its points. Thus a miter at a sharp corner is probably not the cause. - A likely cause is the screen projection of the world points. `push_screen_polyline_runs` projects each point by itself (`interact::project_uv`). - A point behind the eye (`w <= 1e-6`) is dropped, and the run continues to the next point that projects. - A point just in front of the near plane projects to a very large screen position. - Neither case clips the segment at the near plane, so a run can connect two points that are not neighbours on the outline, or go to a point far off the screen. ## Related: the halo that disappears (also in v0.24.0) In v0.24.0, at some angles and zoom levels, parts of the thick stroke disappear, and only the thin depth-tested overlay line stays. The cause is the same projection: a segment with an end behind the eye is dropped. This is older than the wedge. ## Expected The thick pick outline follows the picked edges at each angle and zoom. A segment that crosses the near plane is clipped at the near plane. It is not dropped, and it is not connected to another part of the outline. ## Done means - Each segment of the selected-pick and hover highlights is clipped at the near plane in clip space before it is projected. - A run never joins two points that are not neighbours on the outline. - A test with a picked rectangle seen from a low angle, with a corner behind the eye: - Each stroke vertex stays within the stroke width of the projected (clipped) outline. - No segment of the outline is missing. Found during the test of #2958 (PR #2989). #2989 does not change this code. Proposed labels: `bug`, `P3`, `effort:medium`, `area:ui`, `source:agent`

Threading says it cuts a modelled thread (`threading cuts a MODELED thread (a revolved V section); a smooth bar has none to find`). A real modelled thread from SolidCraft (`solid.thread`, `designation:"M16x1.5"`, `modeled:true`) cannot be threaded either way it is brought in:

A turned part with a modelled helical thread finds the Z axis and threads; or the refusal says plainly that helical models are not read yet and what to model instead.

title: Indexed pockets retain the world stock height as a local cap and report false shank collisions

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

Indexed pocket operations can report a false shank collision with stock.
Found while building the catalog case for #2868, part of #2392.

The original blank spans X/Y -30..30 and Z0..70 mm.
The two side pockets use A+90/B0 and A-90/B0.
Their local top is 30 mm. Their local floor is 26 mm.
The 6 mm EM-0600-4FL cutter has a 15 mm flute length and no holder.
Generation reports shank collisions with uncut stock. Verification holds both operations.

## Cause

At upstream/main 58cb641ca, operation/generate.rs:205-206 computes stock_top_z in world coordinates.
At line 3638, the tilted branch initializes st_local with this world value minus origin Z.
Lines 3659-3666 only increase this value with projected box corners.
The correct local cap of 30 cannot replace the initial world value of 70.
The local shank bottom is about 41 mm at the pocket floor.
It clears the real stock cap of 30, but not the incorrect cap of 70.
The local verification therefore reports a collision.
stock_top_law.rs only rechecks RapidInStock warnings against the exact solids.
It does not recheck ShankHit warnings.

This differs from closed #903, which concerns the tilted band exclusion region.
The conservative box cap for an oblique face is a separate limitation.

## Expected

Compute the stock cap in the coordinate frame of the path under test.
Do not retain a world height as a lower bound for a local height.
Keep true shank collisions blocked.

## Done means

A pin with world Z70 and A+90/B0 uses the projected local stock cap of 30.
The A-90/B0 case has the same result.
A safe shank above the real stock cap passes. A real collision still blocks posting.

Priority: P3. A legal operation is refused; a smaller stock envelope avoids this cap error.
Effort: high. The fix changes collision verification and meets the safety floor.

body:
What happens (v0.24.0, macOS universal release build, `camcraft-cli 0.24.0`):

A user's real two-setup Tormach 770MX project (8 operations, one tool) regenerates and verifies clean - `gate.ok: true`, no problems, no findings, nothing held - but the post is refused:

```
camcraft-cli process sc_logo.camproj -o sc_logo-v0.24.0.nc
camcraft-cli: post: post engine: post script: post output line limit exceeded
exit 1
```

Posting one file per operation (MCP `set_post_options {"per_op": true}` then `post`) is refused the same way, at one operation:

```
post: S1 Notch adaptive + terrace finish: post engine: post script: post output line limit exceeded
```

That operation is a 3D Pocket (offset rings, stepdown 0.15 mm over ~15.5 mm depth, stepover 2.032 mm, T 1/4 in flat) that generates 105,592 moves - one more file than the cap allows. The cap is `MAX_OUTPUT_LINES = 100_000` in `crates/post/src/post/js.rs` (the runaway-script guard of `js_host.rs` PRELUDE `_emitLine`). The other ops are 13,791 + 39,904 + 10,443 + smaller moves, so the whole program is ~170k lines.

Why it is wrong: the guard exists to stop a looping script, but it also refuses a legitimate, verified program, so the user cannot make the part from CamCraft at all (per-op output does not get round it). A Tormach PathPilot control runs files of this size. The message also gives no number and (in `process`) no operation, so the user cannot tell what to change.

Workaround: raise the op's stepdown or split it into two Z ranges (changes the finish the user designed).

Expected:
- A program whose line count follows from its toolpath posts; the guard scales with the input (e.g. a bound derived from the number of moves/operations), or is far higher than any real toolpath, and still stops a runaway script.
- If a limit still refuses, the refusal names the limit, the line count reached and the operation.

Evidence: the user's project (local, not in the repo); a synthetic fixture with a 3D Pocket of >100k moves reproduces it. Found while re-posting the user's showcase parts on v0.24.0 (user goal "the two parts"); before v0.24.0 this project was refused earlier by #1749, so the cap was never reached.

Done means: a verified program over 100,000 lines (pinned by a test with a >100k-move operation) posts through the Tormach post whole and per operation; a real runaway script is still refused, and that refusal names the limit and the operation.

title: A model opened at reduced accuracy posts against its own mesh deviation, with a visible note in the program

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
The maintainer decided on 2026-11-20: widen the verdict tolerance for a model that opens at reduced accuracy. This issue holds that work. Part of #2976.

## What happens

PR #2994 (issue #2976) opens a STEP file whose edges lie as far off their surfaces as the tolerance that the file states. The model is meshed at a coarser tolerance (up to 0.02 mm) and gets the reduced-fidelity flag and a note.

A program on that model cannot be posted. The fidelity law (#864) permits a verdict only while the excess of the mesh tolerance over the import chord is inside `DEV_TOL` (0.01 mm). The measured case: the chord is 0.02 mm, the import chord is 0.005 mm, so the excess is 0.015 mm. The law then has no verdict tolerance, and each operation is refused by name unless its stock to leave covers the excess. A finishing operation thus cannot post. The command `VouchModelFidelity` does not apply, because the chord is a measured value.

The file is legal and it opens. The user has a workaround only for roughing (stock to leave). Thus the priority is `P3`.

## What is wanted

- The verdict tolerance of such a model is the mesh deviation of the model itself, with a hard upper limit (for example 0.02 mm). The limit is a constant that no file can raise.
- The posted program says so: a comment in the program header names the model and the tolerance that the checks used. The UI shows the same fact as a note in plain English.
- The vouch command is not the mechanism for this.

## Safety

The gouge check must stay conservative in the direction that matters: the tool must not cut deeper than the real surface permits.

- The mesh can stand inside or outside the real surface by its deviation. The check must not count that deviation in favour of the tool. State the rule for each direction (a cut into the part, and material left on the part), and why a gouge of the real surface larger than the limit still blocks the post.
- The stock simulation, the keep law, the rest material and the collision checks each read the verdict tolerance. List each reader and what changes in it.
- A model at full fidelity keeps today's law, with no change of any verdict.

## Done when

- A test with a model at reduced accuracy (our own fixture, mesh deviation just under the limit) pins that a finishing operation posts, and that the program header has the note.
- A test just over the limit pins the refusal by name.
- A test pins that a real gouge deeper than the verdict tolerance still blocks the post on such a model.
- Each full-fidelity pin of the fidelity law stays green and unchanged.
- The decision file names the rule, the limit and what the user loses.

## Order

The code needs PR #2994 on `main`. The research does not.

Part of #2976. Refs #2994, #864

title: 3+2 operations: the first-traverse law does not judge the machine table

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:multiaxis
labels.description: 3+2, 5-axis, rotary

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Found by the read-only review of PR #2985 (issue #2901). The PR records the gap in its decision file. This issue tracks it.

## What happens

PR #2985 adds the law `first_traverse_low`: the clearance plane of a milling operation must be above the top of the start stock and of each fixture, because the first traverse starts from an X/Y that is not known.

In a 3+2 frame the law does not read the box of the machine table (`crates/app/src/operation/first_traverse.rs:89-99`). The table box is a slab about 1,000,000 mm wide. Read along a tilted tool axis, its "top" is very large, and each indexed operation was refused. The PR thus skips the table when the frame is tilted. An upright frame still reads the table. The stock and the fixtures are read in each frame.

What stays without a check: the first traverse of each 3+2 operation against the machine table. A tilted clearance plane goes down toward the table on its low side, about 0.36 mm for each mm of travel at B 20 degrees. A real table can thus stand above the plane inside the travel of the machine. That is a collision that passes. Thus the priority is `P1`.

## Possible repair

Clip the table box to the travel of the machine (the machine file has the axis limits) before the corner reading. Then the law can read the table in a tilted frame.

## Done when

- A 3+2 operation whose clearance plane goes under the table top inside the machine travel is refused by name.
- The indexed example operations that post today still post.
- A machine file with no axis limits gives a defined result (a refusal or a note), not a silent pass.

Refs #2901, #2965

title: STEP import refuses Lobe.stp: one edge lies 0.0102 mm off its face, over the 0.01 mm cap

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
The maintainer reported this in chat on 2026-11-20, on build V0.24.0 acd5b02d. He opened `Lobe.stp` (the file is `testdata/models/Lobe.step` in his checkout; it is untracked and stays local: never copy it to GitHub) and got this refusal:

```
import refused: corrupt STEP: solidcore: import_step produced an invalid result: 1 of 1 solid item(s) refused; first #14 at read: pcurves failed on 1 of 14 faces; first: face #230: kernel pcurves: edge 2 lies 0.0102 mm off the face's surface, over the cap of 0.01 mm - re-export the model, or import an STL
```

What happens: the whole solid is refused. The gap is 0.0102 mm, 2 percent over the cap of `MAX_EDGE_GAP_MM = 0.01` mm (`crates/kernel/src/solidcore_trims.rs`, line 40). The file is a legal STEP file.

Expected: a model whose edge gap is this small imports, or the refusal says why a gap of this size is unsafe. A user file must not need a re-export for 0.0002 mm.

Why `P3`: wrong behaviour that a user finds, with a workaround (re-export, or import an STL). It is not wrong output: the refusal is the safe side.

Known facts:
- The cap was set "from data": the largest gap on the fixtures that read is 1.2e-6 mm (decision `docs/decisions/917-solidcore-step.md`). Those fixtures are few. A real exporter gives gaps that are 4 orders of magnitude larger.
- The cap exists to refuse an edge that is a visible step off its face (0.25 mm on a 1 mm part, #917). 0.0102 mm is far below that.
- The file declares its own tolerance (STEP uncertainty). The cap is a fixed number and ignores it.

Research questions (post the answers in comments; file sub-issues):
- What is the gap on the real files we hold? Measure the gap per edge on `Lobe.step`, `fig8.step`, `fillet_corner.step`, `bar_cross_holes.step` and the twisted-flank file. Report the largest value for each file.
- Should the cap follow the file (its declared uncertainty, with a floor and a ceiling), the size of the model, or the machining tolerance of the operation? Name the safe rule and the reason.
- What does the old truck reader do with a 0.0102 mm gap? (`git show 3ffe2338f` has the truck path; the recorded verdicts are in the STEP bench.)
- Can the kernel heal the gap (move the edge onto the face) instead of a refusal, with the move recorded in the import notes?

Safety (AGENTS.md "Prime Directive"):
- A looser cap can accept a model with a small step, and a toolpath on such a model can gouge by that step. Any change needs pins at the new cap and just over it, and the refusal text stays by name.
- This is under the safety floor: `effort:max`.

Done means: `Lobe.step` imports, or its refusal names a defect that is real. The rule for the cap is in `docs/decisions/` with the measured gaps of each file. Pins show a gap just under the new rule is read and a gap just over is refused.

Related: #917 (closed), #2919 (short-name units), #2780 (thread flank speed).

title: STEP model import: the short name of PLANE_ANGLE_UNIT is not read, so an angle in degrees can be read as radians

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Found by the read-only second review of PR #2927. The finding comes from a read of the code. No run proves it.

## What can happen

A STEP file can use the short entity names of ISO 10303-21. The short name of `PLANE_ANGLE_UNIT` is `PLANUN` (public ISO short-name registry, `https://standards.iso.org/iso/10303/tech/short_names/short-names.txt`, line 1554). The solidcore p21 parser does not map this name, and PR #2927 does not add it.

A file that states its angle unit as degrees with the short name then has no angle unit that the reader can find. The reader uses radians. An angle that the file gives in degrees, for example the semi-angle of a cone, is then read as radians. The surface has the wrong shape, and no refusal or note tells the user.

Wrong geometry is wrong output for each toolpath and each gouge check. Thus the priority is `P1` until a test shows the correct angle or a refusal.

## Where

- `crates/kernel/src/solidcore_step.rs`: the rename step that PR #2927 adds for `GUAC` and `SUNT`, and the unit read after it.
- The same registry gives `GC` for `GLOBAL_UNCERTAINTY_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT`. It is not mapped. That changes the tolerance only: check it in the same work.

## What is expected

- The reader reads the angle unit of a short-name file, or
- a file that has an angle unit that the reader cannot resolve is refused by name. An angle is never read in a unit that the file does not state.

## Done when

- A STEP fixture that we made, with short names and a cone whose angle is in degrees, is in `testdata/models/`.
- A test imports it. The cone has the correct angle (checked by a size that depends on the angle), or the import is refused by name.

Refs #2919, #2927

title: Rotary and multi-axis operations: no law judges the first traverse from an unknown X/Y

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1

labels.name: area:sim

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

body:
Found while fixing #2901.

**What happens.** After a tool change the machine does not know its X/Y. The first traverse of an operation can cross any point of the setup. #2901 adds the first-traverse law (`sim::verify::first_traverse_low`). The law applies only to the 2D milling, 3D milling and vertical hole kinds on a mill without a rotary axis, upright or 3+2.

These operations have no such law:
- operations in a setup with a rotary axis (4th-axis wrap and the rotary kinds);
- the multi-axis kinds (continuous 5-axis, swarf, flow);
- the cross drill (radial holes).

Before #2901, the opening rapid started at the WCS origin. The rapid law judged that line by accident. The machine does not travel that line, so the old check did not protect these kinds either. The rapid laws and the simulation judge only the moves that the path contains.

**Expected.** Each of these kinds has a stated first-traverse law, or a named refusal, for its own clearance surface (for example the clearance radius about the A axis, against the stock and the chuck and tailstock).

**Evidence.** `crates/app/src/operation/first_traverse.rs` (`answers`) excludes these kinds. The decision is in `docs/decisions/2901-first-traverse-law.md`.

Done means: for each excluded kind, a test shows that a clearance surface inside the stock or a fixture holds the post by name, or the decision file records why the kind cannot have that collision.

title: Viewport: draw toolpaths and height planes as wide anti-aliased lines, with MSAA and a depth offset

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body: ## Problem The viewport draws toolpaths, height-plane rectangles, region outlines and the other overlay lines as `wgpu` `LineList` primitives (`crates/ui/src/viewport.rs`, `overlay_pipeline`). A `wgpu` line is always 1 hardware pixel wide. The viewport targets use `sample_count: 1`, thus the lines also have no anti-aliasing. The result: - The lines are thin and jagged. On a display with 150 % scale, they are thinner again. - The feed colour (green) has low contrast against the grey stock. It is hard to see the paths and the direction chevrons. - The WCS triad does not have this problem. egui draws it again over the GPU image with a 3 px anti-aliased stroke (#195, `GIZMO_STROKE_PX`). Thus the triad is much easier to see than the toolpath. ## Trial A trial on a local branch (not pushed) rendered `examples/first-part.camproj` through the real viewport pipelines (`gpu_render` test harness). The operation Face1 is open, thus its height planes show. **1. Close view. Before: today. After: 1.5 px wide lines, MSAA 4x, depth offset.** **2. Full view. 1.5 px stays clear when the camera is far. 2 px and 2.5 px made the dense paths into one solid area, thus 1.5 px is the default.** **3. Depth offset. Without it, a wide line that lies on a face is half hidden by the depth test. The line then shows thin and broken. With the offset, the line has its full width.** ## Proposed change 1. **Wide lines.** Draw each overlay segment as a quad that faces the screen (two triangles). The vertex shader extends the quad to the line width in pixels. The fragment shader fades the edges for anti-aliasing. - Use one instance for each segment (36 bytes), and make the 6 corners in the shader. Do not write 6 full vertices for each segment. At the overlay limit (`MAX_OVERLAY_VERTICES`, 512k segments), the trial layout used approximately 135 MB. The instanced layout uses approximately 18 MB, which is less than the current 24 MB. - Extend each end by half the line width and fade the end. Then two lines that meet at a corner (for example, a height-plane rectangle) close the corner and do not overlap past it. 2. **Line width setting.** The default is 1.5 pt. The range is approximately 1 to 3 pt. Multiply the value by the pixels-per-point of the display. 3. **Depth offset.** Move each wide-line vertex toward the eye by approximately 3 line widths of world distance. Calculate the world size of one pixel from the `mvp` matrix (the length of its y row), thus the offset is correct in perspective and in orthographic projection. In perspective, the vertex moves along the eye ray, thus the line does not move on the screen. - Effect: a line that is behind a face by less than approximately 3 line widths shows through. This is a few pixels of depth on the screen, which is much less than a real feature. 4. **MSAA setting: Off, 2x, 4x.** The default is 4x. - All viewport pipelines and the trace composite pipeline (`crates/ui/src/trace/composite.rs`) must use the same sample count. The pass renders into a multisampled target and resolves into the current colour texture. - WebGPU guarantees only 1 and 4 samples. 2x needs the device feature `TEXTURE_ADAPTER_SPECIFIC_FORMAT_FEATURES` and a check of the adapter's sample counts for the colour and depth formats. If the adapter does not support a count, do not show it, or use the nearest supported count and write a log line. - The web build shows Off and 4x only. ## Cost - **MSAA 4x memory.** The colour and depth targets have 4 samples. At 2560×1440, this is approximately 120 MB more GPU memory. At 4K, it is approximately 265 MB. 2x uses half. An integrated GPU is the most sensitive, thus MSAA is a setting. - **MSAA and the traced stock.** The composite writes `frag_depth` once for each pixel. Thus MSAA does not smooth the traced stock edges. Its cost does not change. - **Wide lines.** The overlay uploads only when the scene digest changes (`view_pass::sync_scene`), not when the camera moves. The GPU does approximately 3 times more vertex work and blends approximately 3 to 4 times more line pixels. This is small compared to the model mesh. - Measure the frame time before and after with the `frame_cost` timers, on a large toolpath and on an integrated GPU. Write the readings in the PR. ## Not changed - The geometry, the toolpaths and the posted G-code do not change. This is a display change only. - The pixel goldens (`docs/images/`, `crates/ui/tests/snapshots/`) change at the cut, not in the PR (AGENTS.md "Pixel snapshots are release-lane"). ## Done means - Toolpaths, height planes, region outlines and the other overlay lines draw as anti-aliased lines of the set width. The default is 1.5 pt, multiplied by the pixels-per-point of the display. - A line that lies on a face shows its full width. - The corners of a height-plane rectangle close and do not overlap past the corner. - The MSAA setting (Off / 2x / 4x) and the line width setting persist. An unsupported sample count does not crash and writes a log line. - Tests: - A GPU readback test shows that a line on a face has its full width. - A test shows the instanced buffer size for each segment. - A test shows the fallback of an unsupported sample count. - The PR has the frame-time readings. Proposed labels: `enhancement`, `P6`, `effort:medium`, `area:ui`, `source:agent`

body:
## What are you trying to do

Post a rectangular wire EDM punch to an Agie Classic Cut 2S from the desktop or a command script. The controller needs a linked ISO contour, SBR resource list and SBL job. The generic ISO wire post writes a single program.

## How you imagine it working

Select the native post and a compatible machine. Select the controller separation length explicitly. Write all three files to a new job directory. Refuse an unsupported setup without creating output. The controller applies its resident wire compensation to the nominal contour.

The proposed first case is one vertical rectangular punch in 20 mm stock, with a 0.25 mm wire and a 1 mm separation cut. An offline control accepted a synthetic 40 by 20 mm example. Its graphical check showed a rough pass, three trims and a final separation sequence. This was a software check. A physical machine was not tested.

## Source decision

The proposed writer draws on an independently developed MIT-licensed implementation. Its source notes attribute some interface details to observations of controller examples. The native job uses a resident technology selection. We have not verified a public programming manual for all required call arguments and selection values. No vendor runtime, control image or technology table is proposed for distribution.

Does this reference meet the project's clean-room source rules for an EDM post? If a different reference is required, which published programming reference should we use?

Done means: The project accepts the sources for the post. The desktop and command script produce the same complete native job. Tests pin the supported output, refuse unsupported setups, and preserve an existing destination.

title: 2D Chamfer without picked edges: a bevel on one side and an equal undercut lip on the other side read as a leaning wall

body:
Found by the read-only second review of PR #2940. The finding comes from a read of the code. No run proves it.

## What can happen

PR #2940 exempts a loop from the partly-bevelled refusal of #2887 when the top section is the wall section moved rigidly (`leans` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/chamfer_ride.rs`). That is correct for a wall that leans in a tilted frame.

The two sections are `[-29,31] x [-20,20]` and `[-30,30] x [-20,20]`. They are exact translates, so `leans` is true. The chamfer is then cut all round. It breaks the sharp Y edges and the lip edge. That is the defect of #2887.

The case needs the lip offset to be equal to the chamfer offset within 1e-4 mm. It is not probable, but the result is a cut that the user did not ask for.

## Possible repair

Permit the exemption only when the shift is equal to the shift that the tilt of the operation frame gives. In an upright frame that shift is zero, and this part is refused again.

## Done when

- A test with this part pins the refusal.
- The box under a 10 degree tilt (#2936) still generates.
- The sentence "Thus the new test cannot hide a case of #2887" in `docs/decisions/2936-chamfer-leaning-wall.md` is corrected.

Refs #2936, #2887

generate: MachiningAt { msg: "S1: invalid machining parameters: the edge loop near X35.000 Y20.249 carries a modelled chamfer on only part of its length - it is sharp near X-35.000 Y-16.176 - a chamfer with no picks would cut the sharp part; pick the edges to break", at: Point3 { x: -18.378, y: 35.0, z: 12.379 } }
