title: STEP model import: a file with ISO 10303-21 short entity names can import at the wrong scale

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Found by the read-only review of PR #2918 (comment of 2026-11-20). The finding comes from a read of the code. No run proves it yet.

## What can happen

A STEP file can use the short entity names of ISO 10303-21. The solidcore p21 parser changes some short names to the long names (`SHORT_NAMES`, `solidcore-record/src/step/p21.rs:614-659` at the pinned revision), for example `A2PL3D`, `CRTPNT`, `DRCTN` and `LNGUNT`. It does not change the short forms of `GLOBAL_UNIT_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT` and `SI_UNIT`.

The unit read of the model import (`length_units` in `camcraft-kernel`, and the units module of solidcore) finds only the long name `GLOBAL_UNIT_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT`. Thus a short-name file gives geometry but no unit context. If the reader then uses 1 mm for each unit, a model in inches or metres has the wrong size by a factor of 25.4 or 1000. No refusal or note tells the user.

Wrong geometry is wrong output for each toolpath and each gouge check. Thus the priority is `P1` until a test shows a refusal.

## Where

- `crates/kernel/src/solidcore_step.rs` (`length_units`, near line 244).
- The same defect class in the tool-body read is a blocker of PR #2918 (`crates/geometry/src/step_csys_read.rs:28-30`, `crates/geometry/src/step_units.rs:37-62`). That PR repairs the tool-body read only.

## Not known

- If the reader before PR #2904 (truck-stepio) had the same result for short-name files.
- If a CAD system that our users have writes short names. The form is legal but not common.

## What is expected

- A file that has geometry and a length-unit record, but no unit context that the reader can find, is refused by name. The unit laws of #306 and #689 apply.
- Better: the reader knows the short names of the unit entities and reads the unit.

## Done when

- A STEP fixture that we made, with short entity names and an inch unit, is in `testdata/models/`.
- A test imports it. The result is the correct size in millimetres, or a refusal that names the missing unit context. The result is never a model at 1 mm for each unit.
- The same test set has a metre file.

Refs #917

title: Slot wider than the tool leaves up to 0.86 mm in its round ends, and verify is ok

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What

A Slot with a width larger than the tool diameter leaves material in its two round ends. `verify` reports no problem, and the post is not blocked.

The work on the example case `2d/slots` (#2861, part of #2392) found this.

## How to reproduce

On `main` at `ab9955105`, run this script with a model `slots` (a 100 x 60 x 12 mm block, stock of the same size):

```js
cam.call("add_tool", { catalog: "EM-0600-4FL", holder: "none" });
cam.call("add_operation", {
  kind: "Slot", name: "Slot1", tool: "EM-0600-4FL", source: "slots",
  params: {
    a: [-25.0, 15.0], b: [25.0, 15.0], width: 10.0, stock_to_leave: 0.0,
    top_z: { reference: "top_of_stock", offset: 0.0 },
    bottom_z: { reference: "top_of_stock", offset: -6.0 },
    stepdown: 3.0, stepover: 2.0, feed: 600.0, plunge_feed: 150.0, climb: true
  }
});
cam.generate();
cam.verify();   // ok
```

## What the program does

The tool is 6 mm and the slot is 10 mm wide. The tool centre must stay in a stadium of 2 mm radius around the line `a -> b`. Each level posts three rows:

```
G01 X-25. Y13. Z9. F150
G01 X25. Y13. Z9. F600
G01 X27. Y15. Z9. F600
G01 X-27. Y15. Z9. F600
G01 X-25. Y17. Z9. F600
G01 X25. Y17. Z9. F600
```

The rows touch the round end only at their end points. The tool does not follow the arc between two row ends. The move between two rows is a straight line (a chord), not an arc.

## Measured

A point check of the 10 mm stadium against the tool centre path gives these results:

- The largest leftover is 0.86 mm, on the wall of each round end at 45 degrees, where no move joins two rows.
- The leftover is 0.59 mm at the two corners where a chord joins two rows.
- The total area that is not cut is about 8.9 mm2 for each level.

The straight walls are correct. The rows at `Y13` and `Y17` cut them to size.

## Expected

One of these:

- The Slot cuts its full outline. For example, the tool follows the two half circles of the tool centre stadium at each level.
- The operation reports the leftover as a warning that names the Slot and the largest leftover.

## Workaround

- Use a smaller `stepover`. The leftover becomes smaller, but it does not go to zero.
- Use a Trochoidal slot of the same width. Its last move is a half circle around `b`, and its entry is a full circle around `a`.

## Notes

- The row law is in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slots.rs` (`SlotParams`: "each row reaches the round ends exactly as far as it can").
- The case `examples/catalog/2d/slots` shows the two programs side by side. A fix changes `slots.nc` of that case. Run `cargo xtask catalog --case 2d/slots` with the fix.

title: Opening rapid of a milling path starts at the WCS origin: seat it over the entry point

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

body:
## What happens

Each 2D and 3D milling path starts with a rapid from (WCS X0 Y0, clearance) to the entry point of the operation. The machine never makes this move: after a tool change the X/Y position of the tool is not known.

- The viewport draws a rapid line from the WCS origin.
- The simulation moves the tool from the WCS origin. Between two operations it goes from the end of the first operation to the WCS origin, then to the entry of the next one.
- The fixture checks and the link router judge this move. If the line from the WCS origin to the entry strikes a fixture, `plan_links` lifts the link at the WCS origin. The post then writes `G00 Z<H>` and `G00 X0. Y0. Z<H>`: a real first move to the WCS origin. A fixture at the WCS corner can also give a false refusal or a false fixture hit.

## Where

- `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs:3109-3117`: `path.seat_approach(Point3::new(0.0, 0.0, hl.clearance), [o.x, o.y])` puts the start at the WCS origin (#2382).
- `crates/cl/src/cl/path_approach.rs:30-49`: `Toolpath::seat_approach`.
- `crates/app/src/operation/fixture_route.rs:186-229`: `plan` lifts the link at the start X/Y.
- The seeds: `PathBuilder::approached(Point3::new(0.0, 0.0, p.clearance_z))` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/*.rs` and `crates/motion/src/finishing3d/*.rs`.
- The tests that lock the current behaviour: `crates/app/tests/wcs_start.rs:143-170` (`opens_at`) and `crates/cl/tests/origin_approach.rs:62-99`.

## What is expected

- The WCS is only the reference of the coordinates. No move of the path starts or ends at the WCS origin unless the operation cuts there.
- The opening rapid starts over its own entry point, on the clearance plane: `from.x == to.x` and `from.y == to.y`. It stays a rapid (the approach law of #690 and #697).
- The posted program does not change when no fixture is struck. The current goldens stay byte-identical.
- With a fixture, the link router does not lift a link at the WCS origin. No `X0 Y0` block is posted for it.
- The 3+2 frame case and the yaw case keep their local frame (the call site reads the frame before the seat).

## Done when

- `seat_approach` seats the start over the end X/Y of the opening rapid, not over the WCS origin. Alternative: it is removed and the seeds do the same. Record the choice in `docs/decisions/`.
- `wcs_start.rs` asserts the new law for a face (2D), a 3D finish and a drill, with the WCS at the stock centre and at the stock corner. The opening rapid has no X/Y length, and no move starts at the WCS origin.
- A new pinning test in `crates/app/tests/` puts a fixture box between the WCS origin and the entry. The posted program has no `X0 Y0` block and no fixture refusal.
- `crates/cl/tests/origin_approach.rs` is updated for the new law.
- The posted goldens in `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/` do not change.

Refs #2899

title: 2D Chamfer with no picks on a part bevelled on only some sides: the sharp sides are ridden and the op is refused as a gouge, with no note naming the edges

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
What happens (main 5fdbed9bd, after #2596's fix in PR #2638):

A 2D Chamfer with no picks, on a 60 x 40 x 10 plate that has a 1 mm modelled bevel on the X0 side only, plus a sharp 20 x 10 pocket:

- The generator classifies each top loop whole (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/chamfer_ride.rs:68-69`, one-sided vertex `gap`, line 113). The outer loop counts as bevelled, so all four outer sides are ridden, and the three sharp sides (Y0, Y40, X60) are cut at z 9.2.
- The verifier then refuses the op: `models_a_bevel` (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/wall_anchor.rs:63-71`) fires on any bevel sample, and `crates/app/src/stock_sim_breaks.rs:144` drops all of the op's edge-break credit. Gate: `gouge: program cuts below the model in 840 cell(s), worst 0.74 mm at (1.31, 39.94, z 9.26)`.
- Without the extra collinear vertex on the bevel's top edge, the outer loop reads as sharp (gap 0, `chamfer_ride.rs:68`): the tip rides x = 1 inside the part, and the pocket rim is ridden too. Verify again refuses (1147 cells, 0.74 mm).

So the output is safe: no posted program cuts into a sharp edge. But the user gets a gouge line at a coordinate, not a reason. The op cannot be used without picking the edges, and nothing says that.

Expected:
- With no picks, ride only the modelled bevels, per segment rather than per whole loop, OR refuse at generation with a message that names the partly bevelled loop and asks for picks.
- Classify bevel vs sharp in a way that does not depend on tessellation (two-sided gap, or per segment).
- A note names the edges the op left sharp.

Found by: a blind safety review in a model trial (probes built on wopr against main; no code from the trial is proposed). Related: #2596, PR #2638.

Done means: the 60 x 40 plate with a bevel on one side posts a clean chamfer of that side only (or a named refusal that asks for picks), with and without the extra vertex; a pinning test for both; no change to the all-sharp-part behaviour (#303) or to the verifier's refusal of cuts into sharp edges.

title: Turning profile rides post runs of identical G01 blocks (moves shorter than the output resolution)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:turning

body:
Found during the work on #2394 (example case turning/cone-thread).

## What happens

The Profile Rough and Profile Finish rides contain runs of moves that are shorter than the output resolution of the post. The Fanuc lathe post writes them as identical consecutive `G01` blocks.

Reading: `examples/catalog/turning/cone-thread/cone-thread.nc` (PR for #2394). The program has 1197 lines. 408 of them are a `G01` block that is identical to the block before it. Example, from the finish ride where the nose comes off the collar corner onto the shoulder face:

```
G01 X28.404 Z20. F0.0333
G01 X28.402 Z20. F0.0333
G01 X28.402 Z20. F0.0333
G01 X28.402 Z20. F0.0333
G01 X28.4 Z20. F0.0333
G01 X28.4 Z20. F0.0333
(23 more identical blocks)
G01 X19.812 Z20. F0.0333
```

## Cause

`crates/motion/src/turning/offset.rs`, `profile_offset`: the chord bisection (`settle`) halves the interval toward a kink of the offset curve, where an arc meets a line or a vertical. The samples come closer than 1 micrometre. `out.dedup()` removes only samples that are exactly equal.

## Effect

- The program is correct in position.
- A control can stop for a moment at each zero-length feed block. This can leave a mark on a finished face.
- The program and the project file are larger than necessary.

## What is expected

The ride has no move shorter than a small fraction of the tolerance. Alternatively the lathe post drops a feed block whose words are equal to the last position.

Refs #2394

title: Turning profile offset: a steep fillet chord sends the ride far out of the bar (X354 on a 30 mm bar)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:turning
labels.description: Lathe and mill-turn

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found during the work on #2394 (example case turning/cone-thread).

## What happens

A turned profile has a fillet that is tangent to a shoulder face. The first chords of the fillet are steep in (station, radius). The Profile Rough and Profile Finish rides go far out of the bar at the station of these chords, and come back. Each rung feeds through air.

Reading: a 30 mm bar, a collar of 30 mm diameter to Z20, a 1.2 mm fillet from the shoulder into a cone, insert `TN-1600-0R8`, stepdown 1.0, leave 0.25. The posted rough has, for each rung:

```
G00 X354.326 Z17.2
G01 X48.5 Z17.2 F0.0267
...
G01 X354.226 Z19.2 F0.05
G01 X353.936 Z19.209 F0.05
G01 X131.724 Z19.235 F0.05
G01 X87.392 Z19.278 F0.05
...
```

The rapid radius of the operation is also 177 mm, because it is the maximum radius of the outer rung. The finish ride of the same part goes out to X47.182.

The same model without the fillet (a sharp shoulder) posts a maximum of X48.6.

## Cause

`crates/motion/src/turning/offset.rs`, `profile_offset`, the closure `val`: a segment of slope `b` claims `a + b * (s - s0) + d * sqrt(1 + b * b)` at each station of its own window. That is the offset of the infinite line. For a steep, short segment the tangent point of the ball is not on the segment at these stations. The correct claim there is the circle about the nearer end point.

The first chord of the fillet has a slope of 16.6. With `d` = 10.05 the claim is 167 mm above the segment.

A vertical step is not affected: `segs` drops segments with equal stations.

## Effect

- The path is safe: the ride is too far out, never too deep.
- The program wastes time: about 300 mm of feed in air for each rung.
- On a lathe with a short X travel the limit gate refuses a legal program.
- The bisection toward the spike writes many very short moves (see the related issue about zero-length blocks).

## What is expected

The offset of a segment is limited to the stations where the tangent point is on the segment. Outside them the end point circles make the claim. The ride of a filleted shoulder stays within the nose radius plus the leave of the profile.

## Workaround

Model the shoulder as a sharp corner. The case of #2394 does this.

Refs #2394

title: Profile Finish cannot finish a part with a neck and a modelled thread: valleys and the neck step are read as rest

body:
Found during the work on #2394 (example case turning/cone-thread).

## What happens

A part has a turned profile, a thread relief neck and a modelled thread (V grooves). The Threading operation needs the V grooves in its source model. The Profile Finish operation cannot finish the same model. Its verdict reads each place that the 0.8 mm nose cannot reach as rest, and the post is blocked.

Three readings on the finished model of #2394 (cone 20 mm to 10 mm, neck 8 mm from Z60 to Z63, M10x1.5 grooves from Z63 to Z78, insert `TN-1600-0R8`):

| Profile Finish window | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Z20 to Z78 (cone, neck, thread) | `0.0119 mm gouge, 0.7028 mm rest` (the thread valleys) |
| Z20 to Z60 (cone only, ends at the neck) | `0.0062 mm gouge, 0.2435 mm rest` (the nose stands over the step into the neck) |
| Z21 to Z59 | no envelope warning, but 0.8 mm of the cone before the neck is not finished |

A Profile Rough with `stock_to_leave` 0 on the same window gives the same `0.7028 mm rest`.

Thus no profile operation can cut the thread's major diameter (10 mm) on the model that the Threading operation needs.

## What is expected

One model is sufficient for a turned part with a neck and a thread. The profile finish cuts the major diameter and the cone up to the neck. Material that a later groove or threading operation removes (the neck, the thread valleys) does not block the profile finish.

## Workaround

Import two models on the same axis: the turned blank (no neck, no grooves) and the finished part. The facing and profile operations use the blank as source. The neck groove, the thread and the part-off use the finished part. The case of #2394 does this.

Refs #2394

title: Threading: a pass cannot start in front of the end face - the verdict reads free air as rest and blocks the post

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:turning

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Found during the work on #2394 (example case turning/cone-thread).

## What happens

A thread at the free end of a part cannot start in front of the end face. The threading verdict blocks the post.

- The thread kernel puts a V at each lattice point whose band (centre plus and minus half the insert width) overlaps the window (`crates/motion/src/turning/thread.rs`, `k_hi`).
- The meridian scan (`crates/motion/src/turning/revolve.rs`, `scan`) judges each interval that a band covers. In front of the end face the model radius is 0. The V floor is capped at the crest radius. The scan reads the difference as rest.

## Steps

1. Model a bar with a 10 mm thread diameter, 0.92 mm deep V grooves each 1.5 mm, and the end face at Z78. The last groove centre is at Z77.5.
2. Add a Threading operation with a 1.2 mm wide, 60 degree insert. Set the window top to Z78 or above.
3. Generate.

Result: `finish envelope near move 64: 0.0000 mm gouge, 5.0000 mm rest`. The post is blocked. The band of the last V (Z76.9 to Z78.1) is 0.1 mm past the end face.

A window top of Z81 gives the same result: lattice points at Z79 and Z80.5 are in free air, and the verdict reads them as 5 mm of rest.

## What is expected

A threading pass can start in free air in front of the end face. This is the usual practice: the pass starts some pitches before the part so that the spindle and the feed are synchronised. Air in front of the end face is not rest.

## Workaround

Put the last groove of the model so that the insert band ends exactly on the end face. Each pass then starts inside the part length with a feed plunge (G32 output). The case of #2394 does this: last centre at Z77.4, band Z76.8 to Z78.0.

This workaround is not safe with the G76 cycle. See the related issue "G76 cycle starts inside the part".

Refs #2394

title: Fanuc lathe G76: the cycle starts inside the part, so the control moves the insert into the material at rapid

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:turning
labels.description: Lathe and mill-turn

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Found during the work on #2394 (example case turning/cone-thread).

## What happens

The Threading operation starts each pass at the top lattice point of the thread. This point is always inside the length of the part. A pass cannot start in front of the end face (see the related issue about the threading verdict).

With the post option "Threading: G76 cycle", the Fanuc lathe post writes one rapid to the start point and then the two G76 blocks. The start Z is the top lattice point.

A Fanuc-type control moves the insert from the start point to the depth of each pass at rapid traverse. It does this at the start Z. At that Z the bar is solid. Thus the control moves the threading insert into the material at rapid traverse, one time for each pass.

The G32 output of the same thread does not have this problem. It writes the infeed as a `G01` block at the plunge feed.

## Example

The case turning/cone-thread of #2394, with `set_post_options { "threading": "g76" }`, posts:

```
G00 X30.1 Z77.4
G76 P010000 Q250 R0.17
G76 X8.16 Z63.9 P920 Q250 F1.5
```

The part end face is at Z78. The thread diameter is 10 mm from Z63 to Z78. At Z77.4 the insert (1.2 mm wide) stands above solid material from Z76.8 to Z78.

The golden `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/fanuc-lathe/thread_g76.nc` has the same shape: `G00 X12.1 Z14.` on a bar that continues at 12 mm diameter to Z40.

## What is expected

A G76 cycle starts in free air: in front of the end face, or in a relief groove that is wider than the insert. If the start point is above material, the post refuses the G76 cycle by name. It does not write the cycle.

## Basis

The G76 motion (rapid infeed at the start Z, feed along Z, rapid retract, rapid return) is from the public Fanuc lathe programming manuals. No machine ran this program. A person with a Fanuc lathe or simulator must confirm the reading.

## Workaround

Use G32 passes (the default). The case of #2394 does this.

Refs #2394

title: add_operation refuses a new lead shape: the merge patch keeps the seeded shape

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server and agent tooling (crates/app/src/mcp, camcraft-mcp skill)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What

`add_operation` refuses a 2D Contour whose `params` give a lead shape that is different from the seeded shape. The message does not name the cause.

Found during the work on #2859 (example case `2d/contour-tabs`). Part of #2392.

## Steps

Run this script with `camcraft-cli script` on `upstream/main` 5fdbed9bd. A stock, a model and the tool `EM-0600-4FL` are in the document.

```js
cam.call("add_operation", {
  kind: "2D Contour",
  tool: "EM-0600-4FL",
  source: "contour-tabs",
  params: { lead: { arc: { radius: 3.0 } } }
});
```

## Result

```
camcraft-cli: call: add_operation: bad params patch: invalid value: map, expected map with a single key
```

## Cause (as read from the behaviour)

The tool applies `params` as a JSON merge patch on the seeded parameters. The seeded lead is `{ "linear": { "length": 8.0 } }`. The merged value has the two keys `linear` and `arc`. The lead is an enum with one key, so the parse fails.

## Workaround

Remove the seeded key in the same patch:

```js
params: { lead: { linear: null, arc: { radius: 3.0 } } }
```

## Expected

One of these:

- The patch replaces the lead when it names a different shape.
- The refusal names the field and the cause, for example: `lead: give one shape only (found linear and arc)`.

The same merge applies to `edit_operation` and to each parameter that is an enum with data (`links.approach.lead_out` is one). The fix must cover them.

## Done means

A test in `crates/app/tests/` gives `lead: { arc: { radius: 3.0 } }` to `add_operation` and to `edit_operation` for a 2D Contour. The operation gets the arc lead, or the refusal names `lead` and the two shapes. The `camcraft-mcp` skill says how to change a lead shape.

title: Solidcore STEP mesh: the 2D pocket corner check meets a loop that crosses itself, and three toolpath pins move

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: in-review
labels.description: Fix pushed on a branch with an open PR; merges at the next cut

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

PR B of #917 (branch `issue/917-solidcore-step`) meshes STEP files through solidcore. The new mesh of `testdata/models/Milling-test.step` and `testdata/models/fig8.step` is finer. Three toolpath tests now fail. They pass on the head of #2843 (`eae027d55`). The PR marks them `known-fail #2849`. Their asserts do not change.

1. `lead_approach::the_horizontal_arc_entry_on_the_users_pocket_verifies_silent` (line 247). The stock-source pocket with `Entry3D::Helix` gives these notes:
   - `entry: the horizontal arc entry does not fit (...) - the entry descends onto the pass start without it`
   - `entry: the pass start (-31.878, 8.513) at Z 17.500 is in material and the helix fits only away from the pass start - ramp along the pass instead` (and the same at Z 15, 12.5, 10)
   - `2D Pocket: the check for corners of the stock tighter than the tool did not run (invalid geometry: loop crosses itself) - look at the stock corners around the part`
2. `lead_approach::an_axis_aligned_lead_start_posts_the_users_arc_entry_as_g18_or_g19` (line 131). The contour with `axis_start` gets no vertical arc. Notes:
   - `entry: oblique vertical arc posted as chords - no standard plane`
   - `depth: the ring at (-0.333, -7.491) ends at its floor Z 0.000 - the part is solid below it; levels below skipped (-5.000, -7.000)`
3. `shoulder_adaptive::fig8_outside_containment_with_em0800_and_clearing_kinds_works` (line 312). The last feed ends 31.406 mm from the part outline. The test expects 4 mm (the tool radius). The path verifies clean and posts.

## Safety

No result is silent wrong output. Tests 1 and 2 state each fallback in a note. Test 3 verifies clean. But the corner check in `crates/app/src/operation/keep_law.rs` does not run, and the user sees only the note.

## The defect

The "loop crosses itself" error comes from `Region::normalize` in `crates/geometry/src/geo2d.rs` (line 233). A region that the corner check builds from the new mesh outline has a self-crossing loop. Find which loop it is, and why the solidcore mesh makes it. Then check if tests 1 to 3 have the same cause.

## Done when

- The three tests pass with no change to their asserts.
- The `known-fail #2849` markers are removed.

title: multiaxis: rotary operations ignore face selection - machine full model only

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:multiaxis
labels.description: 3+2, 5-axis, rotary

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
What happens:
Rotary Contour, Rotary Parallel, and Rotary Offset ignore face selection. They always generate toolpath over the full model. A user cannot contain the operation to selected faces.

title: Touching solids: a face bounded only by shared edges, and the feature graph, read the shared edge as non-manifold

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

Since #917, the STEP reader gives each solid of a file its own facets. Two closed solids that touch along a wall can put one mesh edge into 2k facets, k in each direction.

The branch of #917 (PR B, stacked on #2843) adds one rule in `crates/geometry/src/geometry/shared_edge.rs`, `solids_touch`. The slicer (`slice_bodies::closed_solids`) and the winding check (`pick/winding.rs`) use it. The rule passes such an edge when all of these are true:

- the count is even and balanced
- each body uses the edge one time in each direction
- no apex is on the edge line
- each body has a facet on the plane of a facet of a different body

The bodies come from a link over plain edges only (two uses, one in each direction).

The rule fixes the shipped `sample_ap214.step`: it slices, and it reads as outward for Align. Two cases stay open:

1. **A face whose full boundary is shared edges.** Example: two blocks stacked face to face. The contact face of each block links to no other facet of its block over a plain edge. Thus each shared edge sees four bodies that use it one time each, and the rule refuses. Align then refuses the model as non-manifold. The slicer refuses it by name.
2. **The feature graph** (`geometry::feature::features_of_facets`) has its own edge map. It does not use the rule. On `sample_ap214.step`, 216 tangent edge pieces pick apart (`no_pickable_edge_is_a_tangent_piece_of_a_longer_one_in_any_step_fixture`).

## Rules that were tried

- **Radial pairing** (pair each facet with its angular neighbour about the edge). It failed on the sample: the solids overlap, and two facets in the same direction lie on one plane, so the order is ambiguous. It also let two cubes that meet only along one line pass, which is wrong.
- **Wall on a wall** (`solids_touch`, kept). It fails in case 1, because the bodies form before the shared edges are judged.

## Safety

Neither case gives wrong toolpath output. Each is a refusal by name, or an edge that picks in pieces. The pins:

- `shared_face_bodies::welded_non_manifold_solids_are_refused_as_a_model_fault`
- `shared_face_bodies::the_sample_laid_flat_generates_3d_finish_and_pocket_with_no_gouge`

## Wanted

- Link a face that only shared edges bound to its own solid. For example, use the STEP solid ranges (`Mesh::solid_ranges`, `app::mesh_solids`) when the model has them, or pair the coplanar opposed facets first.
- Give the feature graph the same rule.
- Remove the known-fail markers that name this issue.

title: STEP thread flank meshes at 391 K facets (anisotropic plan in solidcore-tess)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

The solidcore STEP path (#917, PR B on `issue/917-solidcore-step`) meshes the four-turn thread flank fixture with too many facets.

The test is `crates/app/tests/import_step_thread.rs`, `a_four_turn_thread_flank_meshes_at_full_fidelity_in_a_bounded_count`.

| Reading | Main (old reader, #1602 division) | solidcore path |
|---|---|---|
| Facets | under 5000 (the pin passes on main) | 391338 |
| Chord | 5e-3 mm | 5e-3 mm requested, replanned at 2.5e-3 mm |
| Debug test time | not measured | 93 s |

The import note is: `STEP sheet #418: replanned at 2.5e-3 mm chord to meet the requested 5e-3 mm measured tolerance`.

## Cause

At the pinned rev, solidcore-tess plans the long, thin helicoid strip isotropically. The plan at a 5 um chord measures over the tolerance. The seam then replans at half the chord (`PLAN_MARGIN`), and the count goes up again. Our seam (`crates/kernel/src/machining_mesh.rs`, `planned`) can only pick the chord. It cannot pick the shape of the division.

## Options

1. An anisotropic plan upstream in solidcore-tess: divide along the strip by the curvature of each direction.
2. A division hint through our seam: pass a per-face step in u and v to the planner, if solidcore-tess gets an API for it.

## Acceptance

The pin `facets.len() < 5_000` in the test above passes, with the other asserts of the test (chord not reduced, longest edge, area, axial gap). Until then, the test has the known-fail marker with this issue number.

Refs #917

title: Windows: tests that read golden/fixture text fail under Git's default core.autocrlf=true (.gitattributes misses post goldens, .mch and .step fixtures)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:low
labels.description: Mechanical, one file, no new logic (issue-worker-low)

labels.name: P7

body:
Found by the new Windows check (Windows 11, Git for Windows defaults: `core.autocrlf=true`), main 380c29b3c, `cargo xtask gate quick`.

## What happens

Git for Windows checks text files out with CRLF by default. `.gitattributes` pins `crates/app/tests/golden/**`, tester kits, examples and `*.sh` to LF, but not every fixture that tests compare byte for byte or parse. Four suites (17 tests) fail on such a checkout, each within a second:

| Suite | Reads | Pinned? |
|---|---|---|
| post `explain_fanuc_family`, `explain_remaining` | `crates/post/tests/golden/explain/*.nc` | **no** |
| app `wire_taper_angle` | `crates/app/tests/edm/wire-iso-fixture.mch` (include_str) | **no** |
| app `import_step_curve_guard` | `testdata/models/box.step` (include_str) | **no** |

Example: `fanuc_explain_golden_preserves_program` - left (generated) ends lines with `\n`, right (golden from the checkout) with `\r\n`; the content is otherwise identical.

## Fix

Pin every byte-compared or parsed text fixture to LF, e.g.:

```
crates/*/tests/golden/** text eol=lf
crates/*/tests/**/*.mch  text eol=lf
testdata/**/*.step       text eol=lf
testdata/**/*.stp        text eol=lf
```

(or one broader rule for `crates/*/tests/**` and `testdata/**`), then `git add --renormalize .`. A unit test in xtask (or a CI-free check) could assert that `git check-attr eol` is `lf` for every file under the golden/fixture dirs.

## Done means

On a fresh Windows checkout with `core.autocrlf=true`, the four suites above pass; `git check-attr eol -- <each fixture>` reports `lf`.

> Issue; P4; Solidcraft has a very good viewport menu, feature we wanna copy is "Shaded with edges, Shaded, Wireframe, Shaded with hidden edges". The "look at" feature, and the graphic settings

This issue is the part of #2818 that its first PR does not include. #2818 permits the split ("If the work is large, split it").

## State of the code

The PR of #2818 adds the Display menu to the viewport toolbar (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/display_menu.rs`). The menu has:

- the four display modes;
- "Look at a face" (one click on a model face or a stock face);
- a Graphics group with "Grid", "Origin axes" and the projection.

## Wanted

Add these entries to the Graphics group of the Display menu:

1. A quality preset: "Performance" and "Quality". A preset sets the switches below. The menu shows which preset is active. If the user changes one switch, no preset is active.
2. "Ground shadow": a soft shadow of the model on the ground grid plane.
3. "Ambient occlusion": darker shading in the corners of the model.
4. "Look at" for a picked plane that is not a model face: a work plane of the WCS, or a construction plane.

- Each switch is view state. It is a direct field write and is never a command. It is saved in `view.json` with the display mode (`camcraft_app::view::ViewPrefs`). An old file without the field loads the default.

## Done means

- A test shows the draw list with the shadow pass and with the occlusion pass, on and off.
- A counter test shows that a still frame builds no shadow data and no occlusion data.

title: Gate: take the default job budget from the machine's core count (not a fixed 6)

labels.name: enhancement

labels.name: P5

body:
Follow-up of #2727 (PR #2788).

## What happens

`xtask/src/budget.rs` sets the gate's job budget to a fixed `DEFAULT` of 6 when `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS` is not set. The batch and release tiers split that budget over at most 3 lanes. On a big machine most cores then stay idle.

Measured on the post-merge runner wopr (Ryzen 9 5950X, 16 cores / 32 threads, 125 GB), head `1da2bcca2` of #2788, warm cache, all green, 929 steps:

| Budget | Batch wall time |
|---|---|
| serial (before #2788) | 73 min |
| default 6 | 30.8 min (load ~15 of 32) |
| `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=32` | **14.4 min** |

Today every runner needs `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS` in its `.env` (wopr 32, uma 16, m3 16, len 8 are set by hand), and a contributor's machine never gets more than 6.

## Wanted

- When `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS` is not set, the default budget is the number of available CPUs (`std::thread::available_parallelism()`), with a floor of 2 and an upper cap (for example 64).
- Optionally a memory guard: no more parallel test lanes than the free memory allows (each heavy suite needs ~2-4 GB), so a 32-thread box with 16 GB does not swap.
- The lane count follows the budget (today at most 3 lanes); the `ISOLATED` steps, builds, ui steps and clippy still run alone with the whole budget.
- `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS` still overrides; the plan (`--dry-run`) prints the chosen budget and where it came from.
- AGENTS.md / the `gate` skill say the default is now the core count (process change: PROCESS_VERSION bump at merge).

## Done means

On a machine without the variable, `cargo xtask gate batch --dry-run` shows a budget equal to the core count (within the cap and memory guard); a unit test pins the default (mock CPU and memory values), the override and the floor/cap; the existing lane tests stay green.

title: STEP import refuses a legal file: a boundary point lies off a twisted B-spline surface

labels.name: bug

labels.name: area:3d

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

labels.name: waiting-for-user
labels.description: Waiting for the reporter's answer; closed after 7 days without one

body:
## What the user sees

The import of a user STEP file with a twisted B-spline flank stops with this refusal:

`a boundary point lies off the surface, outside its knot domain`

The file is legal. A different tool that reads STEP through solidcore opens the same file. The file is private and is not attached.

## Where

- The refusal comes from `Fault::Outside` in `crates/app/src/geometry/import/step_nearest.rs:112`.
- The import path is the truck-stepio path.

## Cause, as found

- The surface is a degree-3 B-spline surface with a strong twist.
- The Newton search for the nearest surface point lands on a neighbouring sheet of the surface.
- The rescue grid has 4 samples for each knot span. On this surface the grid is too coarse to find the correct sheet.
- The defect is of the same class as #1602.

## Possible fixes

- Import STEP through solidcore (#917). This is the full fix.
- Or make the rescue search denser, or make it use the trim boundary.

The work decides between these and records the decision.

## Done when

- A STEP fixture that we made, with a strongly twisted degree-3 B-spline face, imports without the refusal. The fixture is not the user's file.
- A boundary point that is off the surface by more than the tolerance still gives the refusal.
- The import does not become slower by a large factor on the current fixtures.

## Effort

The importer makes geometry. Thus the safety floor applies and the effort is `effort:high`.

**What happens:** the quick tier picks suites from the gate maps. title: Tilt: a project saved after an angle edit by a build with defect #2599 keeps basis 0 with the new angles

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:multiaxis
labels.description: 3+2, 5-axis, rotary

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

PR #2730 fixed #2599: `EditOperationParams` now moves a tilt with `basis_version` 0 to basis 1 when the A or B angle changes.

A project file can hold the defect already. The sequence is:

1. A build before the tilt basis change saved the project. Its tilts have no `basis_version` key, so they load as basis 0.
2. A build with defect #2599 opened the project. The user changed a tilt angle, for example to A0 B180 or A180.
3. That build saved the project with `basis_version: 0` and the new angles.

A build with the fix opens this file and keeps basis 0, because no angle changes in that session. The operation posts with the cut plane turned, as in #2599.

## Source

The read-only second review of PR #2730 found this group of files. The review did not build and did not make such a file. The decision entry `docs/decisions/2599-a180-legacy-basis.md` does not name this group.

## What is not known

- Whether a file can show that it has this state. A basis 0 tilt that was not edited is legal and must keep its output.
- Whether the preview and the post agree for such a file. The review says that they agree, from a reading of the code only.

## What should happen

Decide one of these and record the decision:

- The application finds such a file at load and tells the user, if a safe test exists.
- The release notes name the limit and the manual repair: change the tilt angle and change it back.

Do not migrate all basis 0 tilts at load. That changes the output of legal old projects.

Refs #2599

- Machine: `assets/machines/tormach-770mx-microarc4.mch` (`LoadMachine::from_file`).
- Tool: catalog `EM-0600-4FL` (6 mm end mill).
- Part: `geometry::cube((5, -15, -15), (35, 15, 15))`, imported with `ImportModel::from_mesh("part", ...)`.
- Stock: `StockShape::Box { dx: 40, dy: 50, dz: 50 }` at `Location { pos: (20, 0, -25), rot: IDENTITY_Q }`. The stock is [0, 40] x [-25, 25] x [-25, 25].
- Operation: `seed_params(OpType::Adaptive2D.ordinal())`, source `SrcRef::Entity("part")`, then:
  - `top_z` 16, `bottom_z` 12, `stepdown` 4, `stepover` 3 (all `Height::fixed`);
  - `clearance_z` 40, `retract_z` None;
  - `optimal_load` 0.5 (the other fields are the seed values);
  - area controls `AreaControls { offset: 3.0, ..Default::default() }` through `EditOperationParams::with_area`.
- Tilt: the test ran three poses in sequence in one test: upright (no tilt), then `Tilt { basis_version: 1, a_deg: 90, b_deg: 0, origin: [0, 0, 0] }`, then the same with `a_deg` -90. I do not know which pose was in progress when I stopped the process.

## Readings

- With the seed `optimal_load`, the three poses took about 170 s in total (debug, `--test-threads=6`, other builds on the machine).

- Release: not tested.

- A measurement in release and in debug tells if this is a hang or a slow path.
- If it is a hang: the generator ends, or it refuses the op by name. A test pins it.
- If it is only slow: record the reading here and close it, or file the speed work at the correct priority.

title: Gate: the batch tier runs ~620 steps one at a time - use the release queue's parallel lanes and one parallel prebuild

labels.name: area:build

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
**What happens:** `cargo xtask gate batch` (and every gate built on it: merge trains, post-merge checks) runs its ~620 steps strictly one after another (`xtask/src/exec.rs`, "the one-at-a-time loop"). Each step compiles and links one test binary, then runs it. Linking a large Rust test binary uses about one core.

**Evidence (2026-11-19, merge train on a 16-core Hetzner ccx43, main 409c0b5ab + one PR):**
- 1 h 20 min wall time; load average 2.7-2.8 on 16 cores for most of the run; the provider's CPU graph sits at ~100-300 % of 1600 %.
- At the moment checked: step 623 (`app suites: pocket3d_reach`), one `rustc` at 100 %, nothing else busy.
- `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=16` was set; it scales `-j` and `--test-threads` inside a step, but the steps themselves do not overlap.

The release tier already has parallel lanes (#2057, the longest-first queue of #2461), which took the release gate from 114.6 to 52.7 min. The batch tier does not use them.

**Proposal (two parts, either helps):**
1. **One parallel prebuild:** before the steps, build every test binary the plan needs in one cargo call (`cargo test --no-run -j N` over the planned packages/targets, with the same profile and features the steps use, so the steps reuse the artifacts instead of relinking one by one).
2. **Lanes for batch:** run the batch steps through the release queue's lanes (longest first, sharing the job budget), so several test binaries run at once.

Keep what the gate guarantees today: every step still runs and is logged, a red step still fails the gate, VOID detection is unchanged.

**Done means:** `cargo xtask gate batch` on a 16-core host uses most of its cores during the build phase, and its wall time drops substantially against the same commit (measure before/after on the same machine; numbers in the PR).

Related: #2461, #2057, #2556, #2557.

title: Machine travel check refuses large-radius arcs: it judges the quarter points of the full circle, not the swept arc

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

A 2D Contour around a part of about 1128 x 822 mm does not post. The machine check reports 40+ travel problems. The part, the stock and the work offset (G54) are correct.

```
post blocked - machine grblHAL 3-axis: 40 limit problem(s):
2D Contour1: move 31 reaches 21864.484 in X, the stroke is -3000.000..3000.000;
2D Contour1: move 31 reaches -21346.099 in Y, the stroke is -3000.000..3000.000;
2D Contour1: move 31 reaches -22475.758 in X, the stroke is -3000.000..3000.000;
2D Contour1: move 31 reaches -43516.220 in Y, the stroke is -3000.000..3000.000;
2D Contour1: move 32 reaches 14585.152 in X, ...
... (+284 more)
```

A larger machine does not help. The reported values grow with the arc radius, not with the part.

## Expected

The check judges the points that the arc really passes through. This program stays inside a stroke of -3000..3000, so it posts.

## Evidence

The part's long sides are gentle curves. The 2D Contour cuts them as arcs with very large radii. Values are relative to G54, read from the saved toolpath:

| Move | Radius | Sweep | Chord | Quarter point X+ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 31 | 22170 mm | 0.259 deg | 100.4 mm | 21864.484 |
| 32 | 14740 mm | 0.390 deg | 100.5 mm | 14585.152 |
| 33 | 11037 mm | 0.522 deg | 100.5 mm | 10981.565 |
| 34 | 8814 mm | 0.653 deg | 100.5 mm | 8839.776 |

The quarter point X+ of move 31 is exactly the value in the refusal (21864.484).

| Extent from G54 | X | Y |
|---|---|---|
| Real cut (endpoints + quarter points inside the sweep) | -4.0 .. 1128.0 | -4.1 .. 821.5 |
| What the check uses (all four quarter points) | -22475.8 .. 21864.5 | -43516.2 .. 44333.6 |

## Cause

`crates/app/src/machine/judge.rs` `move_extremes` adds all four quarter points of the arc's full circle, also when the arc does not sweep through them. The doc comment says this is on purpose ("can only over-report"). That is harmless for small arcs. For a large-radius arc it refuses a legal program on every machine size.

The same function is used by the mill stroke check (`machine/mod.rs`) and by `plasma.rs`, `waterjet.rs`, `wire_edm.rs` and `lathe_stroke.rs`.

## Proposed fix

Add a quarter point only when the arc's sweep passes it. Use the start angle, the end angle and `arc.ccw`. A full circle keeps all four quarter points. Count a quarter point that lies on an endpoint. `crates/geometry/src/sketch_data.rs` `bounds` already does this for DXF arcs.

The sweep direction is the same `ccw` that the post writes as G2/G3. Thus the check stays exact and does not hide a violation.

## How to reproduce

1. Mount a 3-axis machine (I used grblHAL 3-axis, with the X/Y travel set to -3000..3000).
2. Import a part whose outline has long, shallow curves (here: a STEP model of 1128 x 822 mm).
3. Put G54 on the part corner and fit the stock.
4. Add a 2D Contour with an 8 mm end mill (EM-0800-4FL). Generate.
5. Post. The post is refused with the travel problems above.

I can share the project file (`.camproj`) privately.

## Related

- #2585 moves `judge.rs` to `camcraft-post`. Its output must not change, so this fix is separate. The second to land rebases.
- #1882 reads `move_extremes` for program bounds and has the same over-reach.

## Done means

- A large-radius arc with a short sweep inside the stroke does not give a travel problem.
- An arc that sweeps past a quarter point outside the stroke still gives a travel problem.
- The same arc in the other direction is judged on its own side.
- A full circle keeps all four quarter points.
- The existing stroke suites stay green (`vmc_stroke`, `machine`, `lathe_stroke`, `lathe_thread_travel`, plasma, waterjet, wire).

Suggested labels (for a maintainer): `bug`, `P3` (a legal program is refused), `effort:high` (safety floor: a travel check), `area:machine`.

title: XYUV wire EDM: map trimmed swallowtails by input preimage to sew rulings consistently across XY and UV

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: area:multiaxis
labels.description: 3+2, 5-axis, rotary

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
Sew XYUV rulings consistently across planes when one plane heals a swallowtail and the other plane does not.

## Context

When XY trims a tight corner fillet or bridges a shallow slot, its offset ring `wu`/`wl` loses arc length while UV keeps the full arc. Pairing directly by trimmed offset arc length (`crates/motion/src/wire_edm/pairing.rs`) shifts rulings out of phase around the contour and can trigger `folds`, `crossing`, or `too_far`. Also, `ruled_widen::away` (`crates/motion/src/wire_edm/ruled_widen.rs`) computes widening directions from unhealed `given` edges, which can reverse steps near a trimmed vertex.

## What this does

- Build a monotone preimage map from each healed offset ring's edge midpoints and vertices back to arc positions on its original input profile `given`.
- Collapse any excised input span `(s_a, s_b)` to the corresponding trimmed intersection vertex `V_trim` so `ArcLength` and `SyncPoints` pairings generate clean cone/fan rulings from `V_trim` to the opposing plane (`pairing.rs` and `ruled.rs`).
- Snap sync points that fall inside an excised corner span directly to `V_trim` instead of shifting across adjacent flanks.
- Update `ruled_widen::away` to derive the outward miter/offset direction from the surviving offset ring segments at trimmed vertices so per-ruling widening does not reverse or tangle.
- Verify all ruled-surface laws (`folds`, `crossing`, `lean_law`, and 33-height `clearance` against the unhealed `product` surface) on the sewn rulings.

## Done means:

- Asymmetric XY/UV shapes (for example a sharp inside corner or tight fillet on XY paired with an open fillet on UV) generate clean fan rulings without phase drift, false folds, or widening reversals.
- `clearance` catches mid-height wall gouges from bridging across a deep slot on one plane and refuses them by name.

Part of #2690

title: XYUV wire EDM: add heal_tolerance to accept bounded 2D swallowtail offsets and report uncut rest

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.description: 3+2, 5-axis, rotary

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
Add bounded 2D swallowtail healing via an explicit `heal_tolerance` parameter on `WireRuled` (`crates/motion/src/wire_edm/`).

## Context

Today `Region::offset_sharp` (`crates/geometry/src/geo2d.rs`) already trims local inside-corner swallowtails and bridges dead-end slots on a single 2D loop. Then `laws::cover` (`crates/motion/src/wire_edm/laws.rs`) refuses any point where `d - k > COVER_TOL` (`0.002 mm`).

## What this does

- Add `heal_tolerance: f64` (default `0.0`) to `WireRuled` (`crates/motion/src/wire_edm/ruled.rs`), distinct from twist `tolerance`.
- Refuse negative or non-finite `heal_tolerance` at the `wire_contour_ruled` door.
- Pass `reach = k + r.heal_tolerance.max(COVER_TOL)` into `laws::cover` on both planes (`ruled.rs` and `ruled_widen.rs`) while keeping `laws::kerf` (`PATH_TOL`) unchanged.
- Measure the worst uncut rest `d - k` and its location when `d - k > COVER_TOL`.
- If `d - k <= heal_tolerance`, accept the offset ring and push a clear uncut-corner note to `Toolpath::notes` naming the worst rest and spot.
- If `d - k > heal_tolerance`, keep the named refusal with the spot, measured depth `d - k`, and stated `heal_tolerance`.

## Done means:

- `wire_contour_ruled` with `heal_tolerance == 0.0` preserves all existing refusals byte for byte.
- Matching tight inside corners and shallow slots within `heal_tolerance > 0.0` generate valid paths with uncut-rest notes in `Toolpath::notes`, and paths still pass `laws::kerf`, `folds`, `crossing`, `clearance`, and `lean_law`.
- Excesses above `heal_tolerance` refuse by name with location and depth.

Part of #2690

title: A file change during an import is missed: the link records the newer digest over the older mesh

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What Happens

`ImportModel::within` (crates/app/src/commands/import_model.rs, #2463) reads and parses the file, then reads the file a second time for its SHA-256. If the file changes between the two reads, the model holds the first bytes and the link records the second digest. The link check then sees no change. That change is never imported.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Link a model to a file, or import the file.
2. Change the file while the import parses it (a large model, one save during the parse).
3. The model keeps the old geometry. Its operations do not go Stale. The status line says nothing.

## Workaround

Save or touch the file once more. The digest differs from the recorded one, and the check imports the file again.

## What Should Happen

Read the file once. Take the digest from the bytes that the parse used. `ImportModel::graded` already takes bytes in hand; use the same path for a file import.

## Source

Found in the review of PR #2563 (head `aef4f610c`), 2026-11-19. The code comment in `within` names the window. The window is one parse time.

body:
Found in the review fix of PR #2659 (issue #2597, blocker B1).

What happens:
- In a whole-model 2D Contour, a ring whose outline grows below Top Z must step down from the stock top (#2597).
- When the stock top is one stepdown or more over Top Z, only a pass at Top Z keeps the first bite of that ring as small as the bite of band 0. So the ring takes Top Z (`upper_levels` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_whole_reach.rs`).
- Band 0 also cuts its ring at Top Z. When the grown ring is closer to that ring than the lead length, the lead of one ring crosses the other ring at the same Z.
- The verifier reports `Crossing` and blocks the post. The result is visible and safe, but a correct part does not post.

Evidence:
- `crates/app/tests/contour_whole_step.rs` case 1 (chamfered island, Top Z 15, stepdown 3.5, linear lead 8 mm) with the stock box `dz` 18.5: `Crossing { moves: [3, 27] }`. Move 3 is the lead-in of the island-top ring at Z 15. Move 27 is a corner of the grown island ring 1 mm outside it, also at Z 15.
- With the stock top 17 (less than one stepdown over Top Z) the grown ring takes Z 13.5 and no crossing occurs. That case is pinned.

Expected: the part posts, and each first bite stays at most the larger of the stepdown and the band-0 bite. Possible ways: cut the grown ring at Top Z in the band-0 emission, or select a lead that does not cross a ring of the same level. Do not hide the `Crossing` law.

Done means: case 1 of `contour_whole_step` with the stock top 18.5 posts with no blocking warning, and each ring still steps down from the stock top. A pinning test covers it.

title: Verify reports a false gouge when a Face row ends near the open outer rim after a lift over a hole

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

A Face lifts over a hole of its region. The row piece beside the hole ends a tool radius off the hole. If the hole is near the open outer rim of the region, that end is less than a tool radius from the rim. Verify law (b) reports the move as `cuts past the finish surface`. The finding blocks the post.

The finding is false. No part material stands above the cut plane at that rim. The outer rim of a Face is open: its rows cross the rim by design.

## Expected

No finding for a Face move whose end is near an open rim. A move near a wall (part material above the cut plane) is still reported.

## Repro

- Part: a plate 40 x 60 x 10 mm centred on the origin (z 0..10). One dia 6 through-hole at (-12, 0).
- Stock: a box 40 x 60 x 12 mm (z 0..12).
- Tool: `EM-1000-4FL` (dia 10).
- Operation: Face, source the part, `holes: lift` (the default), Cut Z fixed 10, stepover 4, clearance 30.

Result on upstream main 1ae4d061f with the fix of #2437 applied: 5 plunges, and `Gouge` findings at moves 15, 18, 27 and 30. Move 15 is the plunge at X -18.227 Y -5 after the lift. It is 1.77 mm inside the rim at X -20.

## Cause (found during #2437)

`sim::verify::section::tangency` reads each law point against all loops of `cx.region` with the distance floor `r - tol`. In `Mode::Boundary` with a model, it does not ask if the region edge is a wall. `wall_gouge` in the same file has that classification for the whole-move reading (a region edge is a wall when the model section holds a probe beside the edge midpoint).

## Workaround

Use `holes: through` or `holes: cut_air` when the holes are air, or use a stock source.

## Notes

- This is a change to a gouge law. It needs a pin that a wall below the model top is still reported.
- #2437 removed the lifts for holes below the cut plane. This defect stays for holes at the cut plane.

**Done means:** a Face that lifts over a hole near the open outer rim has no finding; a test pins it, and a second test pins that a move within a tool radius of a wall is still reported.

title: Sodick wire post: no runnable pass structure for LN1/LN2/LN3 controls (C000 entry, C001 rough, C002 sizing)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Reported by a Sodick wire EDM owner (@spikeypineapple) on #617, 2026-11-16:

> I can say for sure this won't work. It might work on older machines, but it won't run on a ln1/ln2/ln3 control (anything made in the last 20 years).

**What the LN controls expect** (his report): the condition codes follow the passes:
- `C000` - entering the cut (a stable condition, so the wire does not break)
- `C001` - rough cut
- `C002` - sizing / second cut
- `C903` and up - polishing passes

**What the post does now** (`assets/posts/sodick-wire.cps`, main 1ae4d061f):
- writes ONE condition word per operation, the operation's own condition id (`C` + three digits), line 296;
- refuses a condition change between passes (skims), line 186, and sends skims to `wire-iso` instead;
- writes no entry condition before the cut.

So a normal 1- or 2-pass part on a current Sodick cannot be posted as the control expects. Nothing gouges, and the workaround (`wire-iso`, or one operation per pass) exists, so P3 by the AGENTS.md table.

**Scope** (his suggestion): 2 passes first - entry `C000`, rough `C001`, sizing `C002`. Polishing (`C903+`) later.

**Open questions for the reporter** (asked on #617): where in the program each C word goes (on the threading/entry move, at each pass start); whether `C000` is used for every start hole; an example program from an LN control (his earlier AQ600L example on #617 shows a condition table in the header).

Clean-room: no CAM vendor's Sodick post or output is used; only the owner's own description and public Sodick manuals.

Done means: the Sodick post writes the C000/C001/C002 structure for a 1- and 2-pass Wire Contour, pinned by golden programs, and the owner confirms on an LN control (or the open questions are answered on this issue).

Part of #617. Related: #1500 (LN program format), #2130.

labels.name: enhancement

labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
The maintainer asked for this work, in his own words (2026-11-18):

> issue; p4; there is shaded and wireframe today. There should be a shaded with no edges, and wireframe "see thru" as well.

## State of the code

The Browser pane has a "Solids" choice with two modes (`DisplayMode` in `crates/ui/src/state.rs`, radios in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/browser_pane.rs`):

- `ShadedEdges`: flat-shaded faces with the CAD wire over them. It is the default.
- `Wireframe`: faces go to the depth buffer only, so the model reads as a hidden-line drawing. Hidden edges do not show.

## Wanted

Four display modes:

1. **Shaded** (with edges). The current default. No change.
2. **Shaded, no edges.** Faces only. No CAD wire over them. Edges of a picked or hovered feature still show, so that picking stays visible.
3. **Wireframe** (hidden lines removed). The current mode. No change.
4. **Wireframe, see-through.** Every edge draws, front and back, with no hidden-line removal. The model does not hide the stock, the fixtures or the toolpath behind it. Hidden edges may draw in a lighter tone, so the front stays readable.

Details:
- The choice stays one control in the Browser pane. Four radios or one drop-down. Plain English labels: "Shaded", "Shaded, no edges", "Wireframe", "Wireframe, see-through". Tooltips say what each does.
- The mode is view state (a direct field flip, never a command), as today. It applies to the model, the stock and the fixtures in the same way. The toolpath and the simulation stock follow their own rules and stay readable in each mode.
- The setting is saved with the other view settings, if the others are saved. An old file without the field loads with the default.
- Picking works in each mode. In "Wireframe, see-through" a click picks the edge nearest to the cursor, front or back, with the nearest to the camera first. State the rule in the test.
- The renderer builds the edge and face passes once for each geometry change (precalculate and cache; frame target under 10 ms). No per-frame rebuild of the edge lists.

## Constraints

- A UI PR needs before and after screenshots of all four modes in the PR body. Tests assert labels, roles, which mode is selected, the state field and the picking rule. They do not assert pixels. Pixel snapshots are release-lane only and a PR never changes a PNG.
- Update the layout test of the Browser page. Keep each file under about 400 lines.
- `DisplayMode` is also used by the wasm build. The new modes must work there.

## Done means

- A test shows that each radio sets its mode and that the labels exist.
- A test shows the draw list for each mode: faces and edges as listed above.
- A test shows picking in "Wireframe, see-through" with the stated rule.
- The PR has the screenshots.

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
The maintainer reported this in chat (2026-11-18), in his own words:

> bug, when on wcs page, using the set wcs from feature.. u cannot pich each feature correctly.. From a useability feature.. there should be four pick buttons, one for each, z,x,y,origin..  so we dont have to use a dropdown.. it should be clearly a small "table" for it, and then a apply/clear button under the four selections.

## What happens

On the WCS page, the "Set WCS from features" block picks one role at a time through a dropdown. The user cannot pick each feature correctly. The report does not say which pick fails. The worker finds out (see the first steps).

## Wanted

1. A small table with four rows, one for each role: Origin, X axis, Y axis, Z axis.
2. Each row has its own pick button. No dropdown chooses the role. The row shows what is picked (a plain-English name of the feature, not an internal id; see #2403) or "not set".
3. A pick button starts a pick for its own role. A click in the viewport fills that row only. A second pick for the same row replaces it. A row can be cleared alone.
4. Under the table: one "Apply" button and one "Clear" button. "Apply" is enabled only when the picks are enough to define a WCS (for example, an origin, or the axis picks that the existing rules accept). Say in a tooltip what is missing when it is disabled. "Clear" empties all four rows.
5. Apply is one undoable command (the WCS from the setup stays the single source: `setup::wcs_slot`, no second derivation). A conflict between picks (for example X parallel to Z) is refused with a plain message at Apply, not accepted.
6. The page keeps its layout test and its pick tests. UI text is plain English.

## First steps for the worker

1. Reproduce the pick failure. Read `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wcs_pick_row.rs`, `setup_settings_page.rs` and the tests `wcs_page_picks.rs` and `wcs_pick_tests.rs`. Find which pick goes to the wrong role or is dropped (for example a face, an edge, a vertex or a circle centre; see #701, #739, #1562).
2. Fix that defect with a pinning test, in the same PR as the new table or in a first commit.
3. Build the four-row table. Keep each file under about 400 lines.

## Constraints

- AGENTS.md "Everything Is a Command": a pick is ephemeral UI state until Apply. Apply and Clear that changes the setup go through the undoable command. The MCP tool for set WCS from feature picks exists (#937). It stays and uses the same command.
- A UI PR needs before and after screenshots in the PR body. Tests assert labels, roles, enabled state and commands, not pixel values. Update `layout_page_wcs` if it exists.
- Do not use the `fig8.camproj` or `testpart.sc` user files in any test or screenshot.

## Done means

- A test shows that each of the four pick buttons fills its own row, for each feature kind that the page accepts.
- A test shows that Apply writes the expected WCS, that undo restores it, and that a conflicting set is refused.
- A test shows that Clear empties the four rows.
- The PR has the before and after screenshots.

- #2047 (closed) added rotate handles for a part, as slice c of #1198. PR #2185 merged the ring handles and a Rotate button in the floating bar. #2514 lists owed items for them.
- #1198 (open) is the umbrella: "drag a body with gizmo handles (move and rotate), with a floating control bar".
- The maintainer asks for rotate on the movement gizmo itself. So the user must be able to rotate a part without a mode switch or a separate Rotate button.

The first agent that works this issue reads the current viewport code and the build that the maintainer uses. It writes in an issue comment what already exists and what the maintainer cannot reach. If the rotate handles already sit on the move gizmo, the agent says so, names the gap that remains (for example visibility, discoverability or the axis choice), and fixes that gap.

## Wanted

1. The movement gizmo for a selected part shows rotate handles at the same time as the move arrows: one ring for each axis (X, Y, Z of the part frame, or of the setup WCS, as the move gizmo uses).
2. A drag on a ring turns the part about the part centre, about that axis. The preview is live. The turn is shown in degrees. Typing a value is possible, as with the move distance.
3. A modifier snaps the turn to a step (for example 15 degrees). The step is a parameter with a default.
4. Move and rotate go through the undoable commands, one undo step for each drag. The existing move command and its MCP tool stay. A turn about the part centre uses the same command and tool as the existing rotate (`move_model` with a pivot). Add an MCP verb only if the agent surface lacks one (see the optional item in #2514).

- A test shows that dragging a ring turns the part about the chosen axis by the dragged angle, and that undo restores the pose.

title: 3D finishing: CPU facet grid for the drop-cutter support scan (the CPU reference for the GPU filter)

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
Part of #2526 (GPU shader toolpath generation). Slice 1 of 5.

Maintainer order (2026-11-18): "GPU shader issues get priority". Thus this issue is `P4`.

## Why
The ball drop-cutter of 3D finishing tests every facet for each sample. `support_at` (`crates/motion/src/finishing3d/support.rs` lines 368-388) loops over all `Sup` entries with a padded box reject only. Each accepted candidate calls `ball_clear` (lines 132-142), which loops over all facets again. `column_clear` (line 162) does the same. There is no spatial index. The cost is about samples x facets.

The GPU filter of #2526 must match a CPU reference. This slice makes that reference: a CPU grid of facets that the GPU result is tested against. It is also the largest speed gain (estimate in #2526, comment 3/4).

## What
- Bin the `Sup` entries (from `build_sups`, lines 27-50) into a uniform XY grid by their padded box (`xmin..xmax`, `ymin..ymax`, already padded by `r`).
- `support_at`, `ball_clear`, `column_clear` and the fold scan (`edge.rs` `fold_best`) read only the facets of the cells that the query touches.
- The same f64 functions run. The subset must hold every facet whose padded box contains the query point. This keeps the result the same bits.
- Optional, same PR or a follow-up: run the raster lines in parallel with an order-preserving `collect`.
- No GPU code in this slice.

## Prime Directive
- The grid is conservative: a facet goes into each cell that its padded box touches. A bin miss would let `ball_clear` pass a ball that touches a facet. A test pins the superset rule.
- Degenerate input (NaN box, zero-area facet, a box past the coordinate guard) goes to every cell or gives a clean `GenError`. It never panics.

## Pinning tests (CPU reference)
- The 3D finishing goldens in `crates/app/tests/golden/` give the same `.cl` and `.cnc` bytes as before.
- A new motion test: for random sample points over a fixture, the grid query answers the same `support_at` and `ball_clear` values as the full scan.
- A new motion test: each facet whose padded box contains a point is in the grid query of that point (superset law).

## Readings
Measure the time of one large 3D finishing operation before and after (release build). Put the numbers in the PR body.

## Decision entry
Not needed if the change stays inside `camcraft-motion`. No new crate edge, no new dependency.

Effort: `effort:high` by the safety floor (toolpath generation and its gouge certifier).

Done means: the 3D finishing support scan uses a facet grid, the goldens are byte-equal, the superset and parity tests pass, and the PR states the speed readings.

title: Nesting raster 1: conservative bit-packed rasteriser for geo2d regions in camcraft-geometry

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
Part of #2525 (slice 1 of 6). The maintainer set the priority on 2026-11-18: "GPU shader issues get priority".

## What to add

Add a CPU module in `camcraft-geometry` (for example `crates/geometry/src/nesting/raster/`) that converts a `geo2d::Region` to a bit-packed grid of cells. This is the base of the raster nest of #2525. It has no GPU code and no wgpu.

- A grid has an origin, a cell size (integer, in `geo2d::SCALE` units) and a width and height in cells. Rows are packed in `u32` words.
- **Over-approximate mode** (for parts): mark each cell that the region touches. A cell that only touches the boundary is marked.
- **Under-approximate mode** (for the usable sheet): mark a cell free only when the full cell is inside the region. Holes of the region are not free.
- Use integer arithmetic on the `geo2d` integer coordinates only. No float enters the decision of a cell.
- Refuse by name: a non-positive cell size, a grid larger than a stated cell limit, a non-finite input, an empty region where one is required.
- One-line provenance comment: scanline polygon fill and conservative coverage, from Bennell and Oliveira (EJOR 2008) and general computer-graphics literature.

## Why

The raster finds nest positions fast. It is only a first filter. A raster "free" result must be a true "free" result: parts over-approximate, the sheet under-approximates (#2525, research comment 2).

## Notes

- No new crate edge, no new dependency, no decision entry for an edge. Record the cell-size default and the cell limit in `docs/decisions/<issue>-<slug>.md`.
- No MCP tool: this is a kernel module with no command.
- Work that changes nest geometry is under the safety floor: `effort:high`.
- Headless tests only. No GPU.

## Done means

Tests in `crates/geometry/tests/` show:
- For squares, a part with a hole, a thin sliver and a rotated part, each point of the region lies in a marked cell (over-approximate), checked on a dense point sample.
- Each free cell of the under-approximate sheet lies fully inside the region (all four corners and the cell centre inside, and no region edge crosses the cell).
- The same input gives the same bits on each run.
- Each refusal names its reason.

body:
The maintainer reported this in chat (2026-11-18), in his own words:

> and voxel simulation s still broken, no visiable stock removal simulation.

"Still" means that he saw this before. No open issue names it. The nearest closed issues are #2181 (stock removal calculated before playback) and #1516 (stock cut only at the end of each move). The first agent that works this issue checks if one of them is the same defect. If it is, reopen that issue with this report and close this one as a duplicate.

## What happens

The simulation runs, but the stock does not change on screen. The user sees no material removed as the tool moves.

## Expected

The stock shown at each playback position is the stock after all moves up to that position. A cut is visible.

## Not known yet

- The build or version. The maintainer did not name it.
- The model, the stock type and the operation types.
- The engine: dexel column engine (default) or the field engine (`CAMCRAFT_CARRY_ENGINE=field`, #1168).
- If the stock display is empty, frozen at the first frame, or cut but not drawn.

## First steps for the worker

1. Reproduce on the latest `main` with a headless test: build a part and a simple pocket, run the stock simulation to the end, and assert that the removed volume is greater than zero and that the drawn stock mesh differs from the initial stock mesh.
2. Find where the chain breaks: the toolpath moves, the removal engine, the mesh update, the draw call. Use `graphify query` first.
3. Check that the fix does not break the carried-stock and rest-material users of the same engine.
4. Pin the fix with a test that fails without it. Add the case to the `camcraft-sim` or app test set, in the lowest crate that provides it.

## Safety note

A stock simulation that shows no removal hides what the program cuts. This is `effort:high` by the safety floor. If the engine itself gives a wrong stock (not only a draw fault), raise the priority to P1 and say so in a comment.

## Done means

- A test shows visible, correct stock removal after a simple operation.
- The maintainer's view in the GUI shows the removal (screenshots in the PR body, before and after).

title: LinuxCNC and Tormach posts drop a G73 or G85 dwell without a message

labels.name: bug
