body:
## What happens

The LinuxCNC post (`assets/posts/linuxcnc.cps`, PR #2310) writes `G73` for a `PECK` cycle and `G85` for a `REAM` cycle. The LinuxCNC G-code reference gives `G73` and `G85` no P word. When the cycle has a dwell (`PARAM P` > 0), the post writes the cycle block and the dwell is lost. The post shows no message.

`assets/posts/tormach.cps` on `main` has the same pattern for `G73`. Its `REAM` cycle also posts `G85` and drops a dwell.

## Expected

The post refuses a positive `G73` or `G85` dwell by name before it writes the cycle block. The refusal uses the text of the G83 refusal of #2348: `canned cycle G73 (...) dwell is not supported by this post - a <s> s dwell is refused, not dropped; set the dwell to 0`. A cycle with no dwell posts as before.

## Evidence

- Review of PR #2310 (non-blocker 1): `linuxcnc.cps` `onCycle`, the `PECK` and `REAM` cycle maps and the P word line.
- #2356 fixed the same defect on the Fanuc, Haas, Mazak and Doosan posts. #2354 fixed it on Sinumerik.
- #2348 fixed the `G83` dwell on grblHAL and Tormach. PR #2310 copies that fix to LinuxCNC.

## Done means

- `linuxcnc.cps` and `tormach.cps` refuse a positive `G73` and `G85` dwell by name. Check `grblhal.cps` too.
- A test in `crates/post/tests/` pins the refusal for each post, and pins that a zero dwell posts the cycle as before.

title: Machine file: reserved tool numbers (the probe's pocket), so a cutting tool is never given that T number

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: claimed
labels.description: An agent is working on this - see the claim comment

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
## What happens

`add_tool` gives each new tool the lowest unused number from 1 (camcraft-mcp skill: "Assigns the lowest unused tool number in 1-99999"). Many machines keep a fixed pocket for the probe or a tool setter:

- Tormach PathPilot machines: the probe is **T99** by convention.
- A Hurco VMX30U (WinMax): the export on #2566 has `PROBE` as **T1**.
- A FANUC Robodrill (31i-A5): the owner's **T1** is the probe.

On the last two, CamCraft's first cutting tool becomes T1, so a posted program calls the probe for a face or drill operation. Found while making the Robodrill test kit (#2603): its first version faced with T01, and the owner answered "I will not face with my probe!". The kit was renumbered to T12-T15 by hand.

## Expected

- A machine file can name reserved tool numbers, for example `"tooling": { "reserved": [ { "number": 1, "use": "probe" } ] }` (the exact key to be decided).
- `add_tool` and the tool library skip those numbers for cutting tools; a probe tool takes the probe's number.
- `set_tool_number` to a reserved number for a tool of the wrong kind is refused by name (or warned), and verify/post warn when a program calls a reserved pocket for cutting.
- The Tormach machine files reserve T99 (probe); a generic VMC reserves nothing.

## Done means

A test with a machine file that reserves T1 for the probe: the first added end mill gets T2, the probe gets T1, and a program that cuts with T1 is refused by name.

## Open questions for the post

1. **Rigid tapping:** the post writes `G84 ... F` with no `M29`. On a 31i, G84 is rigid without M29 only when parameter 5200 bit 0 is set. Does this machine need `M29 S..` before G84? If so: a post option (or the default) that writes `M29 S..`.

body:
Found by mkinney's QA run p09 (turning on a mill) and narrowed by a verification run on 2026-11-18, CamCraft main `83867fd7`.

On a plain Tormach 770MX, turning operations are correctly refused at `add_operation`. But after `edit_machine {"general": {"kind": "lathe"}}` on the 770MX, turning operations are accepted and the posted program is lathe code (G7/G18, X as diameter) labelled "Tormach 770MX", with no warning that the machine is a mill with a vertical spindle and no lathe axes.

Workaround: use a lathe machine file. Related: #2580 (turning on a mill, the supported way to come).

Done means: a machine-kind edit that contradicts the machine's kinematics (no lathe X/Z, a milling head) is refused by name, or the program header and verify say plainly that a mill was relabelled as a lathe.

title: Flaky test: ui --lib diag_lines_are_tracing_events_at_their_level loses its INFO line in a parallel run

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: effort:low
labels.description: Mechanical, one file, no new logic (issue-worker-low)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
Found during the quick gate of PR #2594 (#2340). The PR does not touch `crates/ui/src/diag.rs`.

## What happens

`diag::tests::diag_lines_are_tracing_events_at_their_level` (`crates/ui/src/diag.rs:124`) fails in some full parallel runs of `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib`:

```
panicked at crates/ui/src/diag.rs:139:9:
the note is an INFO event: 2026-11-18T21:12:45.153099Z  WARN camcraft_ui: gpu: test adapter failed: no surface - trying the next adapter
```

The captured output has the WARN line, but not the INFO line ("headless: test adapter").

Readings on Linux, 12 cores, `--test-threads=10`, tree `v0.24.0` plus PR #2594:
- Full lib run: 1 failure in 3 runs (the quick gate step `ui suites: lib`; then two clean runs, 1170 passed).
- The test alone (`--exact`): 3 passes in 3 runs.

## Suspected cause (not confirmed)

- `diag::info` is one `tracing::info!` callsite. All UI code and all UI tests use it.
- The test installs its subscribers with `tracing::subscriber::with_default`, which is thread-local.
- `tracing` caches the interest of each callsite for the whole process. Other tests run on other threads at the same time, and a new dispatcher causes a rebuild of the cached interest.
- Thus the INFO callsite can be disabled while this test's "info" subscriber is the default on its thread. The WARN callsite stays enabled, which agrees with the output above.

## Expected

The test passes in each parallel run.

## Possible directions (not tested)

- Run the assertions in a separate process or a test binary of its own, so no other test shares the callsites.
- Call `tracing::callsite::rebuild_interest_cache()` after the subscriber is installed, and before each event.
- Serialize the test with the other tests that emit `diag` lines (a lock, as `snapshot_guard` does for the theme cells in #2373).

## Labels

I cannot set labels (no triage access). Suggested by the precedent of #2373: `bug`, `P3`, `effort:medium`, `area:ui`. Filed by an agent session for a contributor, thus `source:agent` also applies.

Done means: `diag_lines_are_tracing_events_at_their_level` passes in repeated full parallel runs of `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib`, and the fix says which runs were measured.

title: refactor(machine): move the per-move limit judgment from app to camcraft-post

labels.name: enhancement

labels.name: P4

body:
Part of #2574 (research answers 4 and 5).

Maintainer request, 2026-11-18, in his words (quoted in #2574):
> "the ability to playback a G-code file in a stand alone Application called camcraft-sim, which opens a g-code file, takes a mch and a cps files as references for making sure it does what it should be doing."

## What is missing
The travel, feed, rpm, tool count and tool size checks exist only in `app` and read the ECS world: `check_ops(world, ...)` in `crates/app/src/machine/mod.rs` (lines 158-175) and the helpers in `crates/app/src/machine/judge.rs`. A stand-alone `camcraft-sim` cannot call them.

## Scope
- Move the world-free half (judge a list of moves, tools and rpm against a `Machine`) to `camcraft-post::machine`. Keep `MachineCheck` and `REPORT_CAP` with it.
- `app` keeps the walk over the operations and calls the moved function. `app` re-exports it.
- Each finding can carry a source location (an operation name in the app, an NC line number in `camcraft-sim`).
- The output of the app check does not change. This is under the safety floor: the existing machine-check tests must stay green with no change of their asserts.
- No new crate edge (`app` already depends on `camcraft-post`).

## Done means
`camcraft-post` has a pure limit judgment over moves with tests in `crates/post/tests/`. The existing app machine-check tests pass with no change of their asserts.

title: sim: generate a loose machine model (blocks and cylinders) posed by axis values

labels.name: enhancement

labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P4

body:
Part of #2574 (research answer 1, option a).

Maintainer request, 2026-11-18, in his words (quoted in #2574):
> "That can generate a "loose" model from the machine file. That would means, table, column, axis, head, spindle etc etc. All joints. "Defined" and loosly generated as a generic block and cylinders design."

## Scope
- Add a module `machine_model` in `camcraft-sim`. Its input is plain data of its own (parts, parent, joint kind, axis, travel, spindle body). `camcraft-sim` gets no edge to `camcraft-post`: the caller maps `MachineTree` (#2583) into the input.
- Make one closed body for each part: a box for a table, saddle or column, a cylinder for a spindle body, sized from `travel`, `spindle_d`, `spindle_len` and the tool station.
- Pose each body for a set of axis values along the kinematic chain (linear and rotary joints).
- Mark each body as "generated". A check that uses it says "judged on a generated model".
- A part with no number to size it gets no body and a named note. It never gets a guessed size without the note.
- Degenerate input (non-finite, zero travel) gives a clean error, never a panic.

## Done means
Tests pin the bodies and their poses for a 3-axis VMC and the tilt-head example at two axis positions each, the "generated" mark, and the refusal of degenerate input.

Depends on #2583 (for the mapping only; the module can land first with its own types).

Part of #2574 (research answer 1).

Maintainer request, 2026-11-18, in his words (quoted in #2574):
> "We want a simulator. That can generate a "loose" model from the machine file. That would means, table, column, axis, head, spindle etc etc. All joints."

## What is missing
The `.mch` file states the machine as a part tree (`kinematics.default.parts`). The reader flattens it: `collect_axes` in `crates/post/src/machine/parse.rs` (lines 35-60) keeps a flat axis list, and `Machine` (`crates/post/src/machine/def.rs` lines 143-255) has no parent chain. A machine model needs the tree.

## Scope
- Add a pure data type `MachineTree` in `camcraft-post::machine`: each part with its `id`, `name`, `type` (`table`, `head`, `linear`, `rotary`), its parent, and the facts the file states (`travel`, `axis`, `pivot`, `offset`, `direction`, the spindle body, the tool station).
- Read it from the same JSON as `parse_mch`, with the same unit scaling and the same unstated-limit law.
- Give the moving side of each axis: the tool side (on the path from the root to the `head` part) or the table side.
- `Machine` and the existing checks do not change.
- A refusal names the part id and the key.

## Done means
`camcraft-post` parses each shipped `assets/machines/*.mch` into a `MachineTree`. Tests pin the parent chain, the moving side and the unit scaling for `3axis-vmc.mch`, `tilthead.mch` and one inch file, and a malformed tree refuses by name.

labels.name: P7
labels.description: Owed polish and small fixes

body:
Asked by mkinney (2026-11-18): "If we get confused by those terms, then so will users/others. Make sure it is clear in the docs."

Two different things are both called "mill-turn":
- **Live tooling / lathe milling:** a lathe (multitasking turning centre) that also mills with driven tools, often with a C axis and sometimes a Y axis. This is CamCraft's built-in "Mill-turn" machine (loads as "MULTITASKING 5-AXIS").
- **Turning on a mill (part in spindle):** a 3-axis mill used as a lathe - the part turns in the mill spindle, lathe tools sit on the table, one work offset per tool (Tormach RapidTurn style). Not supported yet (#2580).

What to change:
- A short glossary box with both terms in the turning guide (`site/content/guide/operations/operations-turning.md`), the machine documentation, and the `camcraft-mcp` skill's machine list.
- Never use a bare "mill-turn" in docs or UI text without saying which one; the ribbon's MILL-TURNING tab names the live-tooling kind.

Done means: the glossary is in those three places, and a search of the docs for "mill-turn" finds no use that leaves the meaning open.

body:
Reported by the maintainer in chat on 2026-11-18:

> when setting up stock using a cylinder you can't change the direction that the cylinder faces. it is along Z. i want it along X or Y or anything in between. there is a "rotation" but i can't seem to figure out what it does.

What happens:

- On the Stock page, the user picks Cylinder stock. The cylinder's axis always stands along Z.
- The page has one rotation field: "Rotation (yaw deg)". Changing it does nothing visible for a cylinder.

What the code does today:

- `StockShape::Cylinder { diameter, height }` in `crates/geometry/src/geometry/stock.rs` builds the mesh along Z. The shape has no axis or direction field.
- The Stock page sends its rotation as a yaw-only quaternion (`quat_from_yaw` in `crates/ui/src/state.rs`). Yaw turns about Z. A cylinder is round about Z, so the field changes nothing for a cylinder. It turns a Box only.
- `SetStock` stores a full rotation quaternion in the stock's `Location`, so the document and the project file can already hold a tilted stock. Only the UI and the meshing follow Z.

Expected:

- The user can set the cylinder's axis to X, to Y, or to any direction between.
- The rotation field does what its label says, or its label says what it does.

Possible workaround today:

- Put a cylinder model in the document, rotate it with MoveModel, and take the stock "From model". This does not help every path: the simulation's field view refuses a stock that carries a rotation (see #2177).

What the work must decide:

- The controls: three axis angles (yaw, pitch, roll) on the Stock page, or an axis picker (Z / X / Y / custom).
- What the field view and the collision checks do with a tilted cylinder stock (#2177 closed one case of this refusal; a tilted primitive needs the same review).
- Wording: rename or explain the current "Rotation (yaw deg)" field.

title: sccache: crates with a build script, and solidcore below them, miss the cache in each new worktree

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
Found during the idle-box Linux measurement of #914 (https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/914#issuecomment-6991514439). Part of the #900 build cycle work.

## What happens

A fresh worktree with a warm sccache cache reaches its first app test no faster than a build without sccache. On a 12-core Linux box: 274 s with a warm cache, 264 s without sccache. The #900 goal is 3x faster.

`cargo build --timings` of a warm run (282 s wall):
- `solidcore 1.0.1` compiles for 216 s, on the critical path.
- All `camcraft-*` units together take 41 s. The first one starts at 250 s.

`solidcore` is a cache miss in each new worktree:
- The sccache hash key of `solidcore` changes with the worktree (`94ef89da...` in one worktree, `78bb5f5e...` in another). The tree and the flags are the same.
- In the same worktree, `cargo clean -p solidcore` and a rebuild gives a hit in 3 s.

The crates that miss in a new worktree are the crates with a build script, and all crates that depend on them:
- Build scripts: `serde`, `serde_core`, `thiserror`, `num_traits`, `crc32fast`, one `proc_macro2` variant.
- Dependents: `serde_json`, `flate2`, `miniz_oxide`, `rayon`, `spade`, `solidcore`, `solidcore-record`, `solidcore-ops`, `solidcore-step`, `solidcore-convert`, `solidcore-tess`.

The `.rmeta` of these crates is not the same in two worktrees (for example, `libserde-aab1de1362e9bc28.rmeta` has a different md5). This agrees with an `OUT_DIR` below each worktree's own `target/`.

`SCCACHE_BASEDIRS` (sccache 0.18.0) with the two worktree roots does not change this. `serde`, `thiserror` and `solidcore` stay misses.

## Expected

A fresh worktree with a warm cache does not compile `solidcore` again. Each worktree compiles only our own crates (the #900 intent).

## Possible directions (not tested)

- Make the build-script crates give the same inputs in each worktree, so that sccache can hit them.
- Share the compiled dependencies between worktrees in a different way. Note: AGENTS.md forbids a shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.
- Make `solidcore` cheaper in dev builds (for example, its `opt-level`), and measure the effect on the suites that use it.

## Environment

Linux (Manjaro), 12 cores, 32 GB RAM, rustc 1.98.0, sccache 0.18.0, `upstream/main` `c605e5687`. At `7cab31eea`, the dev profile, the `solidcore` pin and the sccache code in `xtask/src/exec.rs` are the same.

## Labels

I cannot set labels (no triage access). Suggested: `P7`, `effort:medium`, `area:build`. Filed by an agent session for a contributor, thus `source:agent` also applies.

Done means: a fresh worktree with a warm sccache cache gets a cache hit for `solidcore`, and the time to the first app test is measured and posted against the #914 numbers.

body:
Asked by mkinney (2026-11-18): "Can you create a p3 doc issue for that tools export. If you can import tools, add that too. I might want to import tools for future tests on hub."

## What a Tormach user has today

PathPilot can export and import its whole tool table as a `.csv` file (Tormach 770MX operator manual UM10587, section 7.6.4 "Import and Export the Tool Table"): **Offsets tab -> Export -> type a name -> save to a USB drive**; **Import** on the same tab loads a `.csv` back. PathPilot Hub has the same Offsets tab.

CamCraft today:
- imports and exports tool libraries only as `.camtools` (`import_tool_library`, `export_tool_library`, #355, #899);
- writes a setup's tool list as a generic CSV for a spreadsheet (`tool_list_export.rs`, #389) - not PathPilot's column layout;
- has no docs page that tells a Tormach user how to get his machine's tools into CamCraft.

So a user re-types every tool (number, diameter, length, description) to make posted programs match the machine.

## What to do

1. **Docs** (site guide, Tormach section): how to export the PathPilot tool table (the steps above), how to bring it into CamCraft, and how the tool numbers map to `T<n>` in the posted program. Same page: the reverse, for PathPilot Hub tests.
2. **Import:** read a PathPilot tool-table `.csv` into the document's tools (or a `.camtools` library): tool number, diameter, length/offset, type and description where the file has them; the user completes what PathPilot does not store (flutes, flute length, holder). One undo step; an MCP tool (or a format option on `import_tool_library`); refuse by name a row it cannot read.
3. **Export (for Hub and the real machine):** write the document's tools as a PathPilot tool-table `.csv` that PathPilot's Import reads, so a Hub test or a real job starts with the same tool numbers and diameters as the posted program.

## Open point

The exact PathPilot CSV columns are not in the manual. mkinney will export his 770MX tool table; that file is the sample to build and pin the parser against (tests with a recorded `.csv`, no machine needed).

Done means: a docs page with the export/import steps; an import that reads the sample file into tools with the right numbers and diameters, pinned by a test; an export that PathPilot Hub imports (checked once in Hub).

title: Contour tabs: the bridge check compares only neighbouring cuts

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
## What happens

The bridge check in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/tab_bridge.rs` came with PR #2486. It compares only two neighbouring cuts: the cut before a tab and the cut after it.

The check reads only the last `W + D` of the walk before the tab. It reads only the first `W + D` of the walk after the tab. Lead-in and lead-out moves are included.

A different cut can come closer than the tab width. The check does not read that cut. Two cases are known:

- A U-turn of the same ring. A later part of the ring comes near the tab.
- A different ring at the same level.

The reviewer of head `613ba4abf` says that the tab then holds through a strip that is narrower than W. Main had the same limit before PR #2486. The decision file `docs/decisions/2480-tab-bridge-width.md` records this limit.

## Cases seen in the build review (not confirmed as tab necks)

- A 60 x 7 mm inside slot, W = 3 mm, 3 mm tabs. Two cut runs are 2.06 mm apart. The output has no note. The reviewer says the ring is almost a line here, so the distance is across the slot. The reviewer did not confirm a tab neck.
- An inside L-shape with Perpendicular, Arc or Tangential leads. Lead cuts on the two walls of a 14 mm arm come within 0.07 to 3.4 mm of each other. The cuts are in scrap material, far from the tabs. The reviewer says this was present before PR #2486 and is not a bridge failure.

## First step

Write a shape-mask test in `crates/motion/tests/common/shape_mask.rs` (see AGENTS.md, "2D toolpath shape-mask tests"). Use the U-turn case and the second-ring case. Measure the narrowest bridge.

- If no bridge is narrower than the tab width, post the result on this issue. Keep P3.
- If a bridge is narrower than the tab width, raise this issue to P1. AGENTS.md sets P1 for unsafe output.

## Smaller points

- [ ] `SLACK = 1e-6` (`tab_bridge.rs:77`) has no margin for arc chord error. The reviewer found no bridge under W in a probe, but says the margin is small.
- [ ] With a picked start, the windows grow backward only (`tab_bridge.rs:104`, `128-129`). If the first window grows past the pick, the first keep no longer starts at the pick. No note says this. `contour.rs:307-309` then checks `lead_held` on a keep that is not at the pick. The reviewer says this is not a gouge. Add a `tabs:` note, or a refusal by name.
- [ ] No test has more than one tabbed level. The tests in `crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_bridge.rs` use TAB_H = 1 and a stepdown of 2. The reviewer's probe with three levels gave a correct result. Add a test with more than one tabbed level.

## Done means

- The shape-mask result is posted on this issue.
- Each smaller point is fixed, or has a `tabs:` note or a named refusal, with a test that pins it.

Refs #2480
Found in the reviews of PR #2486.

title: Post: classic Grbl 1.1 (3-axis mill): no canned cycles, no M6, 80-character blocks

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
## Request

Add a post for classic Grbl 1.1 (3-axis mill). Many small routers and hobby mills run Grbl 1.1 on an Arduino-class board. The `grblHAL` post (#710) writes words that Grbl 1.1 refuses, so it is not a replacement.

## Differences to the grblHAL post

From the public Grbl 1.1 documentation (the "Commands" and "Interface" wiki pages, behaviour only):

- No canned cycles. Grbl 1.1 has `G80` but not `G73`, `G81`-`G89`. The post must expand drill, peck and bore cycles to `G0` / `G1` / `G4` moves.
- No `M6`. A tool change is `M5`, a retract to a safe Z in machine coordinates (`G53 G0 Z...`), then `M0` with a comment that names the tool. `T` is written in a comment only.
- No `G43 H`. The length offset is `G43.1 Z...` or nothing. Default: write no length offset (the user zeroes each tool), and write `G49` in the preamble.
- No `O` program number. No `G41` / `G42`. No `G98` / `G99`.
- `G4 P` is in seconds.
- Line buffer of 80 characters: keep each block short. Comments are `( )` only. Do not write comments with nested brackets.
- Coolant: `M7`, `M8`, `M9` only. Other coolant kinds are refused by name.

## Acceptance

- A built-in post `Grbl 1.1` and a machine file `grbl-3axis.mch`.
- Goldens for contour, pocket, drill (expanded), peck (expanded), bore with dwell, two tools.
- A test that each posted line is 80 characters or less, and that no unsupported word (`G8x`, `M6`, `G43 H`, `G41`, `G42`, `O`) is posted.

I can do this work in a PR from my fork.

body:
The work of #1649 carries a flipped X and a flipped Y into the posted program. A flipped Z is still refused by name, at the post gate and in the post engine (`post::wcs_flip`).

The maintainer's words (2026-11-17), quoted in #1649: "the ability to flip axis from a positive to negative is fundamental and should not be blocked.. posting and generation should take it into consideration rather.."

Why Z is not carried yet:
- Tool-length compensation (G43) adds the tool length in the controller's +Z. On a flipped Z, the program's +Z goes into the work.
- The canned cycles (G81-G89) read the R plane and the retract (G98/G99) in the controller's Z. A mirror changes which side is "up".
- The clearance and retract heights of each script assume that +Z leaves the work.

Open questions:
- Is a flipped Z a real machine setup (a part under the spindle face, a tool that points up), or only a WCS on a fixture face? The answer decides if the post mirrors Z or refuses with a clearer reason.
- Which dialects can state a negative tool-length direction (G43 versus G44)?

Done means: a flipped Z either posts a program that a controller reader with the flipped axis traces on the CAM path (the equivalence test in `crates/post/tests/wcs_flip.rs`), or the refusal names the exact reason and the decision is recorded. The setup sheet, the travel check and the viewport envelope follow.

body:
What happens: a model does not remember the file that it came from. `ImportModel` keeps the name, the mesh and the import settings only (`crates/app/src/commands/import_model.rs`). When the source file changes, the user must import it again by hand.

Expected:
- An imported model keeps its source path and the SHA-256 of the file that it read. The `.camproj` file saves the two values. A project that has no values still opens.
- While the project is open, CamCraft checks the source file of each model. When the file has a new hash, CamCraft imports it again through `CommandKind::ImportFile`, under the same model name. The existing update path marks the operations Stale.
- CamCraft never regenerates a toolpath or posts G-code because of this. The user does that.
- A source file that is missing or that CamCraft cannot read does not change the model. The status line says so by name, one time.
- The user can turn off the update for a model ("Unlink").
- An MCP tool reads and sets the link.

Why: Solidcraft proposes "Send to CamCraft" (Solidcraft RFC 0001, phases 1 and 3: https://github.com/tangency-labs/solidcraft/blob/main/docs/rfcs/0001-craft-bridge.md). Each save in Solidcraft writes the `.sc` file again. With this issue, CamCraft updates the part after each save.

Depends on: the issue for opening a model file from the command line (#2462).

Done means: a test changes a source file and finds the model updated and its operations Stale; a test finds an unchanged model when the file is missing; a `.camproj` round trip keeps the link; an older `.camproj` opens.

body:
## What happens

A Face operation with a **model** source and Cut Z = top_of_model (z 15) is refused at the post with 16 blocking findings `move N cuts past the finish surface`. Nothing in the part is above z 15, so one flat pass at z 15 cannot touch it. The QA run saw the path lift over each of the 4 through-holes (rapids around them in the render); the 16 findings come in pairs on those moves (2, 9, 12, 19, 22, 29, ...). The same op with `source: "stock"` is clean and posts.

## Expected

A flat pass at z 15 over the whole stock top (through-holes below the cut plane play no part), clean verify.

## Repro (MCP)

**Part (p01-flange):** 6061 plate 100 x 60 x 10 mm centred on the origin (z 0..10), a 60 x 30 x 5 mm island on top (z 10..15, R5 corners) with a 1 x 45 deg chamfer on its top edges, 4 x dia 6 through holes at (+-42, +-22), a 10 mm wide x 3 mm deep slot across the +X end (x 35..45, floor z 7). Stock: box fitted to the model with +2 mm on top (100 x 60 x 17, z 0..17). WCS G54 at the stock's min-X min-Y top corner, world (-50, -30, 17). Machine Tormach 770MX, post Tormach PathPilot.

`add_tool {catalog: "EM-1000-4FL"}`; `add_operation {kind: "Face", tool: "EM-1000-4FL", source: "flange", params: {cut_z: {reference: "top_of_model", offset: 0}}}`; `generate`; `verify`.

## Evidence (upstream main abe24ff09)

verify: 16 findings, all `blocks_post: true`, moves 2, 9, 12, 19, 22, 29, 32, 39, 62, 69, 72, 79, 82, 89, 92, 99: `move N cuts past the finish surface`. With `source: "stock"`: no finding.

Either the hole lift dips below z 15 on its way down (a real gouge in the generated path, caught) or the finding is false; the fix should say which. P3: verify blocks it and the stock source is a workaround, but the user is told the part gouges.

Found by the QA swarm (SolidCraft v0.44.1 + CamCraft v0.23.0, part p01-flange). Re-checked on upstream main abe24ff09.

**Done means:** Face on a model source above through-holes posts one flat pass with no lifts and no findings; a test pins it on a plate with through-holes below the cut plane.

title: Update check in the title bar: show "Update available" and install the new release when the user clicks it

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
Asked for by Mike (collaborator) on 2026-11-18: SolidCraft shows "update available" in its title bar; a click downloads the latest version and installs it. CamCraft has nothing like it - a user only finds a new release on GitHub.

Wanted:
1. **Check:** at start (and at most once a day), read the latest release tag from GitHub (`api.github.com/repos/NeoTech/Camcraft/releases/latest`). No account, no telemetry; a setting turns it off; offline or rate-limited = silent, never an error dialog. Never in the browser (wasm) build.
2. **Show:** a small "Update available: vX.Y.Z" item at the right of the title bar, next to the version (#352). Its tooltip names the version and links the release notes.
3. **Install on click** - the hard part, because the app is running:
   - Download the asset for this platform (Windows zip/installer, macOS, Linux tar/AppImage, FreeBSD) to a temp folder and check its SHA-256 against the release (the release needs a checksum file - today it has none) before anything runs.
   - Unsaved work: ask to save first (the usual unsaved-changes prompt); never drop work.
   - Replace and restart: a running exe cannot be overwritten on Windows. Usual pattern: quit, let a small helper (or the installer itself) swap the files and start the new version; or rename the running exe aside and put the new one in place, then restart. Package-manager installs (AUR, Homebrew, a .deb) are not self-updated: show "update available" with the command to run instead.
   - Failure at any step leaves the old version working and says what failed.
4. Never auto-install without a click; never download in the background without the setting allowing it.

Done means: on Windows and one of macOS/Linux, a build that is one release behind shows "Update available", a click updates it and restarts on the new version with the project reopened; a corrupt download (bad checksum) is refused with a message and the old version still starts; with the setting off or offline, nothing is shown and nothing fails.

Clean-room note: this is ordinary desktop-app behaviour (no Autodesk material involved). SolidCraft (our sister project) is a reference for the user experience only.

body:
The maintainer reported this in chat on 2026-11-17, with three screenshots of the tool page in Properties:

> Mjor useability bugs; Confusing and... heck

> The tool body editor is confusing.. body saids import body, but there is no way of picking a holder. which i have to open profile todo

> And once you apply a holder, (not profile) it will be popping up as a 3D vizualization.. that makes zero sense..  Tthe properties for a tool should not have the tool body and profile editor in the properties panel, that should open in its own modal like the old editor did.. But the old editor, still exists and should be retired..  As this is just doubling down on the confusion

**What the screenshots show**
- The tool page in Properties has the side preview, then the tabs "Body" and "Profile", then "Apply".
- The "Body" tab has only "Import body..." and "Clear body". It has no control to select a holder.
- The holder library ("Holder library", gauge length, projection, "Apply holder") is at the bottom of the "Profile" tab, below the profile table and a second preview.
- The page has two "Apply" style buttons at different levels: "Apply profile", "Apply holder" and "Apply".

**What is wrong**
- A user who wants a holder looks on "Body" and finds no holder control.
- "Apply holder" opens a 3D view of the tool. That view is not expected in the Properties panel. #2017 has the rule: one side preview, no second 3D preview.
- The Properties panel is too narrow for the profile table and the previews.
- The old tool editor window is still in the program. Two editors for one tool confuse the user.

**Requested behaviour**
1. The tool page in Properties has the tool settings only (layout: #2014), one side preview, and one button that opens the tool shape editor.
2. The tool shape editor is its own modal window, as the old editor was. It holds the body import, the profile table and the holder selection.
3. The holder selection is the first thing that the user sees for a holder. It is not below the profile table.
4. No 3D view opens when the user applies a holder. The one side preview draws the result (#2017).
5. The old tool editor window is removed. Each entry point that opened it opens the new window.
6. Each change goes through the same undoable commands as today. The MCP tools do not change.

**Related**
- #2014: the property grid for the tool settings.
- #2017: one side preview that draws the checked holder shape.
- #2016: a tool holder references a library entry.

Done means:
- Properties shows no body or profile editor.

body:
### What are you trying to do

I picked the shipped grblHAL machine for a setup that posted with Fanuc. The setup kept Fanuc, and nothing suggested the grblHAL post. A `.mch` file cannot say which post goes with it. `post_offer` offers `default_post_for(kind)` only when the current post does not serve the machine's kind, so for every mill the offer is Fanuc. The pairings exist only as comments in `MACHINES`. #1915 and #1918 expect `default_post_for` to map machines to their post, but it takes only the kind.

### How you imagine it working

- An optional key, for example `controller.post: "grblHAL"`, names a post in `BUILTINS`. Without the key, nothing changes.
- `validate_text` refuses, naming the key, a name not in the registry and a post that does not serve the machine's kind.
- When the mounted machine names a different registry post than the setup's, the existing offer banner suggests the named post. Taking it goes through the existing undoable post command. A mount still never changes the post by itself, and a `.cps` file post is never offered over (#343, #388).
- The shipped machines whose pairing is already written down state their post (Tormach, grblHAL/Sienci, TinyG, Makera, Doosan, Haas, the sinker template). The generic ones state none. `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` documents the key.
- `Machine` is `#[serde(default)]`, so an older reader drops the field. That loses only the offer, never a posted program, so I propose no `PROJECT_VERSION` bump.

Question: should this live in the `.mch` file or in a table next to `MACHINES`? I'd choose the file, so a user's own machine can state its post too. Either way it should fit #924's registry move.

**Tests:** grblHAL mounted over Fanuc offers grblHAL, and taking the offer then undoing it restores Fanuc. A machine without the key offers as now, with the existing lathe-over-mill test unchanged. A `.cps` post is never offered over. The validator refuses an unknown name and a post of the wrong kind. Every shipped machine validates.

Not in scope: a `.cps` path in the machine file, or post options in the machine file.

Related: #1915, #1918, #924, #611. I'd like to claim this and open a draft PR once it is triaged.

title: Flaky test: ui --lib parallel run races on process-global theme / colour-vision cells

body:
What happens:

A full parallel run of `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` fails.
A serial run (`--test-threads=1`) passes. The failing test differs each run.
In one run `law_tests::gizmo_tests` fails twice (colour-scan law tests at
crates/ui/src/law_tests.rs:155 and :247, "one bright and one dimmed X").
In the stashed-WIP baseline run six other colour-scan tests fail
(path_tests, preview_tests, path_lines). Serial runs of those same suites
pass.

Evidence:

- Full parallel run, 795 passed, 2 failed:
  law_tests::gizmo_tests::a_moved_origin_shows_axes_and_triad_together
  law_tests::gizmo_tests::each_triad_is_labelled_with_its_own_offset_name
- Baseline run (WIP stashed, branch head without the uncommitted changes),
  787 passed, 6 failed:
  law_tests::path_tests::selecting_the_operation_brings_its_path_up
  law_tests::path_tests::show_all_dims_instead_of_hiding
  law_tests::path_tests::the_path_wears_the_colour_vision_palette_and_off_restores_it
  law_tests::preview_tests::picks_are_pinned_in_the_world_not_the_window
  law_tests::preview_tests::selecting_an_operation_outlines_its_cut_region
  path_lines::tests::the_mark_follows_the_colour_vision_palette_and_the_dim

Suspected mechanism:

The suite mutates process-global cells in parallel frames while
colour-scan law tests read them. Candidates:

- theme::set_current / theme::current: a live OnceLock RwLock, one cell per
  process (crates/ui/src/egui_app/theme.rs); state.rs writes it on each
  frame (crates/ui/src/state.rs line 4103).
- Colour-vision state set through app commands and read by the colour-scan
  law tests.

The structural tests already guard their mutation with
snapshot_guard() (crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests.rs:1926). The colour-scan
law tests do not appear to guard their reads.

What should happen:

The parallel run must be deterministic. A fix: guard every read of the
process-global theme / colour-vision cells with snapshot_guard(), or
serialise those suites. Then pin it with repeated parallel runs (goal:
0/30 failures across repeated full parallel runs).

Done means:

- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` passes in repeated parallel runs
  (>= 3 runs, 0 failures each).
- No `#[test]` count is lost; no test is ignored or deleted to achieve this.

Part of: none (follow-up found during the #1696 report-button work).

title: Rotary Parallel finishes both end faces of the model to the axis: on a bar held in a chuck that is a cut through the bar, and no setting limits it

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:multiaxis
labels.description: 3+2, 5-axis, rotary

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found while writing the continuous 4-axis walkthrough for #1904 (Tormach 770MX + microARC 4, stacked on PR #2342).

**What happens.** Rotary Parallel lays the bar down and runs the finishing raster over the whole model, end faces included (`crates/motion/src/multiaxis/rotary.rs`, `rotary_parallel`). Each end face is finished down to the fitted axis. On rotary work the bar is held at one end (chuck) or both (chuck and centre), so the chuck-side "end face" of the model is inside solid bar. The pass there is a groove one tool diameter wide, cut from the skin to the centreline: it parts the bar.

**Evidence.** `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.camproj` on the #1904 branch: a cylinder model 0.680 in across from X-1.25 to X0, a Box stock from X-2 to X0, a 1/8 in ball tool. The posted program (`examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.nc`) feeds the tool tip at X-1.3125 down to Z-0.029 (Z is the radius from the A centreline), with the stock box going on to X-2. Pinned by `continuous_4axis_part::the_pass_cuts_the_chuck_side_end_face_to_the_centreline`.

What stops it today, and what does not:
- A tool whose flute is shorter than the depth is blocked at post: "shank/holder at move N collides with the uncut stock" (pinned by `a_short_flute_is_blocked_at_the_chuck_side_end_face`, 1/2 in flute). Good.
- A tool with a long enough flute (5/8 in here, or the catalog `BN-0600` default of 15 mm) posts with no warning.
- No setting keeps the pass off an end face. **Bottom Z** is a floor in the laid frame, not a radius: at 0 it keeps only the half of the bar within about 81 degrees of the top and still cuts the end faces to the axis. **Top Z** / **Clearance Z** are radii for the links. There is no axial window (Rotary Contour and Rotary Offset read heights as stations; on a bar lying flat those are inert).
- The kit golden of PR #2342 (`wrap_rotary_parallel_microarc4.nc`) has the same shape: its stock ends where its model ends, so CamCraft sees air where the real bar goes on into the jaws.

**Expected.** A way to finish the turned surface only: an axial window (from/to stations along the fitted axis), or an option to leave the end faces, so the pass stops at a shoulder. Until then, a named warning or refusal when an end-face pass enters stock that goes on past the end of the model.

**Workaround.** None for a real cut on a held bar. The #1904 guide page runs the program as an air cut only and says why.

Priority note: filed as P3 (wrong behaviour with no silent gouge of the part: the stock is cut, the model is not). The maintainer may read "parts the bar off with no warning" as P1.

Done means: a Rotary Parallel job on a bar that goes on past the model's chuck-side end either leaves that end face alone by a setting, or is refused or warned by name; a test pins it; the #1904 guide page drops its "air cut only" limit.

title: Post: a generic LinuxCNC mill post (3-axis), separate from the Tormach PathPilot post

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
### What are you trying to do

I run a 3-axis mill on LinuxCNC 2.9 (Remora controller, `M6` remapped to an automatic tool changer) and would like to post from CamCraft straight to it. There is no plain LinuxCNC post today. The Tormach PathPilot post is the closest, but it carries Tormach assumptions, so its output has to be checked and hand-edited before it is safe on a stock LinuxCNC machine. #435 / #495 is one example: the retract assumed machine Z0 is the top of travel.

### How you imagine it working

A generic LinuxCNC mill post (e.g. `linuxcnc.cps` plus a `linuxcnc-3axis.mch` machine), written to the RS274NGC dialect as LinuxCNC documents it, with no PathPilot-specific codes. LinuxCNC machines differ a lot from one another, so the machine-specific parts would be options rather than fixed:

- **Retract and tool-change position:** `G53 G0 Z<value>` with a user value (machine Z0 is not always the top of travel), `G28`/`G30`, or none.
- **Tool change:** `T<n> M6` then `G43 H<n>`, with an option to leave out `G43` when the `M6` remap applies the tool length itself.
- **Path blending:** `G64 P<tolerance>` with a user value, or `G61` exact path.
- **Program start/end:** a safe block (`G17 G90 G40 G49 G80`, units, work offset); end with `M5 M9` and `M2` or `M30`; optional `%` delimiters.
- **Drilling and tapping:** `G81`/`G82`/`G83`/`G73`. LinuxCNC's rigid tap is `G33.1`, which needs a spindle encoder, so an option to refuse or expand taps on a machine without one.
- **Arcs:** `G2`/`G3` with incremental IJK (LinuxCNC's default `G91.1`), helices allowed.
- Comments in parentheses, no line numbers by default; spindle `M3`/`M4 S`, coolant `M7`/`M8`/`M9`.

Happy to run posted programs through a LinuxCNC 2.9 sim and air-cut them on my machine, and report back.

title: Windowed UI slows down as operations are added, and the frame rate drops when a toolpath is selected (3 user reports; headless stays fast)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Reported by a user on Discord (f1inch), relayed by the maintainer's collaborator on 2026-11-16; filed by an agent:

> "after i add a second operation after faceing the camcraft gets so damn slow that i cant work with it."

The user shared the project privately. It is not attached here.

## The project (shape only)

- Project version 61, 17 MB on disk.
- One model of about 45,000 triangles (8.4 MB of facets).
- One setup, one box stock, one tool (4 mm router bit).
- Two operations: `Face1`, then `2D Contour1`.
- Machine: a hobby router file (FoxAlien WM-3020), grblHAL post.

## Readings (headless, release build of main 3580f3888, Linux)

| Step | Time |
|---|---|
| `open_project` | 0.1 s |
| `generate` 2D Contour1 (forced) | 1.0 s |
| `generate` Face1 (forced) | < 0.1 s |
| `verify` | 0.2 s |

So project load, generation and verification are fast. The slowness is in the windowed shell: the redraw, the scene rebuild, the toolpath or stock display, or the simulation. #164 (closed) found a similar pattern: one CPU core at 100% in the window while `camcraft-cli process` took under a second.

The project also has two problems that are not this defect:
- The model was saved before mesh fidelity was recorded (v58 or older), so the gouge check blocks the post until the model is imported again.
- `Face1` moves go outside the machine stroke (X to -47.5, Z to -4, stroke X 0..290, Z 0..70): 626 limit problems.

A large number of findings can make a UI list slow. Check if the window rebuilds or paints all 626 findings each frame.

## What is not known yet

- Which action is slow: select an operation, regenerate, rotate the view, or play the simulation.
- The user's CamCraft version, operating system and GPU (the paths suggest Linux).
- If one operation is fast and two operations are slow.

## Done means

On a fixture with the same shape (a model of about 45,000 triangles, a Face and a 2D Contour, and several hundred findings), the windowed UI stays responsive: a frame cost close to the one-operation case, no CPU core held at 100% when idle. A test pins the cost that caused it (for example the scene or findings rebuild count for each frame).

title: Nesting: add 2D NFP and bottom-left-fill true-shape placer in camcraft-geometry

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
Add a deterministic 2D true-shape nesting kernel in `crates/geometry/src/nesting/` (no ECS, no world).

## Sources and clean room

Write this module from published literature and CamCraft code only:
- Bennell and Oliveira, *The geometry of nesting problems: a tutorial*, EJOR 2008.
- Burke, Hellier, Kendall, and Whitwell, *A new bottom-left-fill heuristic algorithm for the two-dimensional irregular packing problem*, Operations Research 2006.
- Burke, Hellier, Kendall, and Whitwell, *Complete and robust no-fit polygon generation for the irregular stock cutting problem*, EJOR 2007.
- Reuse `crates/geometry/src/geo2d.rs` (`Region`, `Loop`, `Point2`, `Region::offset_sharp`) and `crates/geometry/src/geo2d/sweep.rs` (`Region::sweep`).
- Do not read or adapt code from HSMWorks, Autodesk Fusion, WAM, SVGnest, or Deepnest.

## Scope

- Define clean input and output structs in `crates/geometry/src/nesting/`:
  - Sheet input: width, height, `edge_margin`, `cut_width` (kerf or router cutter diameter), `part_gap`, and `allow_parts_in_holes`.
  - Part input: stable part id, quantity, outer loop, hole loops, optional open chains, default cut side (`Outside`, `OnLine`, `Inside`), `rotation_mode` (`Locked`, `Orthogonal`, `FixedStep(deg)`), and `allow_mirror`.
- Inflate each part before nesting so separate cuts keep at least `part_gap` of uncut material between cut edges:
  - Inflate `Outside` outer loops by `cut_width + part_gap / 2`.
  - Inflate `OnLine` outer loops by `cut_width / 2 + part_gap / 2`.
  - Inflate `Inside` outer loops by `part_gap / 2`.
  - Buffer standalone open chains via `Region::sweep` (`cut_width / 2 + part_gap / 2` for `OnLine`, `cut_width + part_gap / 2` for side cuts).
  - Support router single-slot clearance mode (`part_gap >= cut_width`) when adjacent outside profiles share a single cutter-width channel.
- Shrink the usable sheet inward by `edge_margin` (plus outer `cut_width` clearance) via `Region::offset_sharp`.
- Compute No-Fit Polygons (NFP) and Inner-Fit Polygons (IFP) on the `geo2d::SCALE` (1-micron) grid.
- Place parts with deterministic Bottom-Left-Fill (BLF):
  - Sort parts by decreasing area first. Break ties by part id and instance index.
  - Try candidate rotations (and mirroring only when `allow_mirror` is true).
  - Place small parts inside usable closed holes (`IFP(hole_usable, part_inflated)`) when `allow_parts_in_holes` is true.
  - Open new sheets when parts do not fit on active sheets.
- Report `sheet_count`, per-sheet placed counts per part (`placed_counts`), total placed vs requested quantities, per-sheet and overall `utilization_pct` (`sum(part_net_area) / sheet_area * 100.0`), `waste_region` (`sheet_region.difference(&union_of_cut_footprints)`), used sheet bounds, and an explicit `unplaced` list with refusal reasons.
- Add the one-line provenance comment at the module head.

## Done means

Unit tests in `crates/geometry` nest irregular parts, parts with holes, and swept open chains deterministically across 1 and multiple sheets, report exact per-sheet part counts and `utilization_pct`, place a small part inside a large part hole with full clearance, confirm zero overlap among inflated footprints, verify waste `Region`, and refuse non-finite, negative, or oversized inputs by name.

Part of #2156

labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found during the work on #2004 (PR #2013, round 7).

## What happens

A 3D Pocket on a blind hole whose floor is between Top Z and the first level gets no floor level. Example: depth 3 mm at stepdown 4 mm. With PR #2013 the operation is refused with "nothing to machine". Before PR #2013 the operation made one pass at Top Z in the air and did not cut the hole.

The test `blind_floor::a_blind_pocket_never_enters_solid_under_any_ladder` pins the refusal.

## Expected

The operation cuts the hole at its floor in one level, as 2D Contour does after PR #2013 (`contour_depth.rs`, `ladder` with `top`; pin `a_blind_hole_shallower_than_one_stepdown_is_cut_at_its_floor`). No cut is deeper than one stepdown. No move enters the solid below the floor.

## Workaround

Set a stepdown that is not more than the depth of the hole.

## Safety

This work is under the safety floor. It changes the toolpath and the posted G-code of a 3D Pocket on a shallow blind hole.

## Done means

- A test shows that a blind hole of depth 3 mm at stepdown 4 mm is cut at its floor, with one level.
- `a_blind_pocket_never_enters_solid_under_any_ladder` stays green with its no-gouge assert unchanged.
- The verify gate is silent on the result.

body:
The maintainer asked for this in chat on 2026-11-15. His words: "Issue, on Geometry tabs, under Boundaries.. there should be selection for faces and edges that is "do not touch".. and he calculation should avoid to gouge them at all costs."

## What is missing

An operation has no way to name model faces or edges that the tool must not touch. The user cannot protect a finished surface, a datum face or a sharp edge from a later operation.

## What to do

1. Add a "Do not touch" selection to the Boundaries group of the Geometry tab of an operation.
   - The user picks faces and edges in the viewport.
   - Each picked item shows as a row with a remove button.
   - The viewport shows the protected items in a different colour while the operation is selected.
2. Store the selection on the operation. The change goes through an undoable command (AGENTS.md "Everything Is a Command"). The command ships with its MCP tool.
3. Add a clearance parameter (default 0, the stock to leave still applies). The tool stays this distance from each protected item.
4. Each generator that the operation type uses keeps the tool clear of the protected items. This includes the cutting moves, the lead moves, the link moves and the plunges. The check uses the full tool: flutes, shank and holder.
5. The verify gate checks each generated move against the protected items. This check is independent of the generator.
6. If a move touches a protected item, the operation is refused or marked "incomplete" with a diagnostic that names the item. The post is blocked. The program is never posted with such a move (AGENTS.md "Prime Directive: Never Crash, Never Gouge").
7. If a protected item is also in the machining selection of the same operation, refuse the selection when the command is created. Say which item is in the two lists.
8. The project file stores the selection. Say in the PR if older builds refuse the new file.

## Scope

- First slice: the selection, the command, the MCP tool, the verify check and the refusal, for one 2D and one 3D operation type. The PR names the two types.
- Later slices: the other operation types. File one issue for each family (2D, 3D, multi-axis, turning, wire).
- Reference material is public machining literature and published user documentation at behaviour level only (AGENTS.md "Clean-Room Protocol"). Write the labels in our own words.

## Safety

This work is under the safety floor. It adds a gouge law and can change posted G-code for an operation that has protected items. An operation without protected items must give the same toolpath as before: pin that.

## Done means

- The Geometry tab has the "Do not touch" selection under Boundaries, with pick, list and remove.
- Undo and redo restore the selection. The MCP tool sets and reads it.
- A test with a protected face next to the cut region shows that no move comes nearer than the clearance.
- A test with a protected face that the selected region cannot avoid shows the refusal, with the item named, and a blocked post.
- A test shows that an operation without protected items gives a toolpath that does not change.
- The structural UI test asserts the new rows and their labels.
- The user guide describes the selection and the refusal.

body:
Part of #2007.

Maintainer in chat, 2026-11-15: "That tool editor issue is a P3".

## What happens

- A tool keeps its own holder as `holder_d`/`holder_len` (`crates/tools/src/tools.rs:203-204`).
- A library holder is copied, not referenced. `SetToolBody::library` (`crates/app/src/commands/tool_body.rs:155-169`) writes the library outline into the tool as a drawn spun body. The tool keeps no link to the library entry.
- The holder fit is thus sized for each tool by hand.

## What to do

1. Add a tool key `holder: {entry, gauge_len, projection}` that names a library entry (`holder_library::find`, `crates/tools/src/holder_library.rs:345`).
2. Resolve the reference to a `HolderProfile` in the one seam: `tool_body::judged`, `stack` and `digest` (`crates/app/src/tool_body.rs:173-224`). Each collision law and the simulation (`sim_tool_body.rs:196-197`) then read the same shape.
3. Keep the #828 floor for a machine-default holder.
4. Migration: an old drawn library copy and an old `holder_d`/`holder_len` cylinder load as a custom holder with the same shape. Use the version step of the cutting-data sub-issue (`PROJECT_VERSION` 62, `.camtools` 2), or take the next one if that sub-issue is not merged.
5. A reference to an entry that does not exist refuses the file by name. It never falls back to a different holder (see #808).
6. Fill the holder fields from the entry. The user does not size them.

This changes the shape that collision checks and simulation read: `effort:max` by the safety floor.

## Done means:

- A tool with a library holder stores the reference, not a copy.
- `judged` and `stack` give the same bands for a referenced holder and for its old copy. A test pins this.
- An old project and an old `.camtools` file load with no change to any collision result. A test pins this.
- An unknown entry name refuses the file by name.
- The `set_tool_holder` MCP tool (#799) writes the reference.
- The PR is `feat!` with a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer.

Order: after the layout sub-issue. The Weldon sub-issue needs this one.

title: Depth ladder: decide between a remainder last step and equal steps

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P7
labels.description: Owed polish and small fixes

body:
The depth ladder of the depth-stepping operations keeps the remainder in the last step. Some users expect equal steps.

What happens:

- The shared level law `camcraft_motion::machining2d::cut_levels` steps down by the full stepdown from Top Z.
- The last level ends at Bottom Z exactly. The last step is the remainder.
- Example: Top Z 20, Bottom Z 2, stepdown 5 gives the levels `[15, 10, 5, 2]`. The last step is 3 mm. The other steps are 5 mm.

The other choice:

- Equal steps: the same number of levels, `ceil(span / stepdown)`, and each step is `span / count`.
- The same example gives four steps of 4.5 mm: `[15.5, 11, 6.5, 2]`.
- Each step stays at or below the stepdown. The load on the tool is more equal, and the last pass is not a light rub.

Where it came from: found while fixing #2004 (the ladder now starts one stepdown under Top Z). The fix kept the remainder and recorded this choice in `docs/decisions/2004-top-z-level.md`, decision 7.

Notes:

- This changes posted G-code of each depth-stepping operation (safety floor: `effort:high`).
- By the project rule "CAM choices are parameters", equal steps is an operation parameter with a default, not a silent change of the law.
- The callers are listed in the audit table of the PR for #2004.

Done means:

- A decision says which ladder is the default, and if the other is a parameter.
- If a parameter is added: it is on each depth-stepping operation, it is undoable through `EditOperationParams`, it has an MCP field, and a test pins the levels of the two modes.

title: Tool editor overhaul: labels left, cutting data by material, one preview, holders from the library

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
The maintainer asked for this in chat on 2026-11-15, on v0.21.0. His words:

> The tool editor page needs a re work, Input fields sitting left of the input, cutting data by material should be default behavior and the default "value" is what we have in the catalog now. We can have a material called "Unknown" that is the default value.  Why there is two previews of the tool is also strange. One drawn profile of the tool and the holder picked should be enough. The holder library, should remove the parametric holder values and "fill them in" with the values from the library.. There is no need for having a Weldon for each "sized tool".. a weldon is a weldon, and whatever tool will fit it.
> In general the Tool editor needs a complete overhaul.

This is an umbrella issue. Research it, then file one sub-issue for each part, and close this issue.

## Parts

1. **Layout.** Put each label on the left of its input field, in a property grid (see the Fusion-style dialog rule: collapsible groups, tooltips).
2. **Cutting data by material is the default.** Each tool has cutting data (speed, feed, stepdown, stepover) for each material. The current single set of values becomes the data of a material named `Unknown`. `Unknown` is the default material. Existing tool libraries and project files load with their values moved to `Unknown`, with no loss.
3. **One preview.** The editor shows one drawing: the tool profile and the holder that the user selected. Remove the second preview. (See #2005: the body and the spun profile draw over each other.)
4. **Holders come from the holder library.** The user selects a holder from the library. The holder values (diameter, length, gauge length) come from the library entry and are not typed into each tool. Remove the parametric holder fields from the tool.
5. **A holder is not sized to a tool.** One holder entry (for example a Weldon holder) serves each tool whose shank fits it. Do not keep one holder entry for each tool size. The fit check (shank diameter against the holder bore) must give a clear refusal when a tool does not fit.

## Questions for the research

- The tool library and project file format change (parts 2, 4, 5). Give the migration and the version bump. This can be a breaking change.
- How the collision check and the simulation get the holder shape after part 4. They must use the same shape that the preview shows.
- Where cutting data by material connects to the operation: the operation uses the material of the setup stock, or `Unknown` when the stock has no material.
- How this joins #2002 (tool settings in Properties, catalog in its own panel). Decide one layout for the two issues.

## Related

#2002, #2003, #2005, #93, #743, #808, #898

## Done means

Each part has a sub-issue with a priority, an effort label and a "Done means" line. This issue lists them and is closed.

Implement native AI provider transport, secret handling, and transport-level offline enforcement in `crates/app`.

## Scope
- Gate native sockets, threads, and OS keychain calls under `#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]` so `crates/ui` continues to build on `wasm32` (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/shell_web.rs`).
- Support public cloud endpoints (`https://` only):
  - Anthropic Messages API
  - OpenAI Chat Completions and Responses APIs (GPT and Codex models)

- Support OpenAI-compatible local endpoints (`localhost` / `127.0.0.1` / `[::1]`):

  - Unsloth Studio (`http://127.0.0.1:8888`)
  - LM Studio (`http://localhost:1234/v1`)

- Store API keys only in the OS keychain (`keyring` crate) or environment variables (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`). Never write secrets to `prefs.json` (`crates/app/src/prefs.rs`) or project files. Reject plain `http://` when sending keys off localhost.

- Use only public provider specifications and update `assets/ui/LICENSES.md` for new third-party crates.

Done means: Fake loopback HTTP server tests verify every provider wire format and Ollama capability detection, `prefs.json` stores zero keys, offline mode blocks non-loopback hosts, and `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` builds cleanly.

title: Post: add RichAuto DSP A11 3-axis router post (richauto.cps) with conformance goldens

labels.name: enhancement

body:
Add a built-in 3-axis router post for the **RichAuto DSP A11** controller in `assets/posts/richauto.cps`. Register it in `BUILTINS` in `crates/app/src/posting.rs` and pin it in `crates/app/tests/conformance.rs`.

## Context

Issue #1907 confirmed that mkinney's friend runs a **RichAuto DSP A11** handheld controller. Common Laguna Swift (`4x4`, `4x8`, `5x10`) and Grizzly CNC routers (`G0894`, `G0931`, `G0895`) also use this controller.

CamCraft's existing posts (`assets/posts/grblhal.cps`, `fanuc.cps`, `carvera.cps`, `tinyg.cps`) do not run safely on a RichAuto A11:
- `grblhal.cps` emits `G91.1`, `G94`, `G53 G0 Z...`, `T<n> M6`, and canned cycles. RichAuto A11 uses the pendant `AbsCntr` menu switch (`Off` = incremental) instead of `G91.1`, and basic router firmware can reject canned cycles or `G91.1`.
- `fanuc.cps` emits `%`, `O0001`, `T.. M6`, `G43 H..`, `G49`, `G91 G28 Z0`, and `G84` tapping.

## Specification (OEM manuals only)

1. **Units and file format:** default to `mm` (`G21`) to match RichAuto's internal metric math and avoid `G20` scale errors. Write `.nc` ASCII files with parentheses comments `(...)`. Omit `%`, `O` program numbers, and `;` comments.
2. **Preamble and arcs:** write `G21`, `G90`, `G17`, `G40`, and `G80`. Omit `G91.1`, `G94`, `G43`, and `G49`. Emit incremental `I`/`J`/`K` matching `AbsCntr = Off`. Handle `G54` cleanly (`G54` default or document `Read G54` vs `Ign G54` in post notes; handle or refuse multi-WCS safely).
3. **Spindle and warm-up:** write `S<rpm> M3`. Add a configurable spindle dwell property (`G04 P<ms>`, default `0`) so the post works alongside the pendant `Spindle Delay` setting. Document 8-step `S1`-`S8` VFD wiring in post comments.
4. **Drilling and tool changes:** expand all canned drill cycles (`G81`, `G82`, `G83`, `G73`, `G86`, `G89`) to plain `G0`/`G1` moves (using the pattern in `assets/posts/carvera.cps` and `tinyg.cps`). Refuse mid-program tool changes on the initial 3-axis manual slice (or lift Z cleanly and write `M0` with `(CHANGE TOOL T<n>)` rather than bare `T<n> M6`).
5. **Refusals and footer:** refuse `G84` tapping, `G41`/`G42` cutter compensation, and probing. Retract Z to clearance height in work coordinates, stop spindle (`M5`) and coolant (`M9` if active), and end with `M30` (no trailing `%`).

## Rules

- Clean room: use only RichAuto DSP A11 OEM documentation, RS-274 / ISO 6983 standards, and CamCraft repository patterns (`assets/posts/AGENTS.md`). Do not read or copy Autodesk, HSMWorks, or third-party CAM posts.

## Done means

- `assets/posts/richauto.cps` exists and registers in `BUILTINS` in `crates/app/src/posting.rs`.
- `crates/app/tests/conformance.rs` passes for `RichAuto DSP A11` across all mill goldens and refuses `G84`, `G41`/`G42`, and probing by name.
- Posted `.nc` output uses `G21`, incremental `I`/`J`, expanded drilling moves, `(...)` comments, safe Z retract, and `M30` with no `%`, `O` headers, `G91.1`, `G43`, or `G49`.
- Decision entry added under `docs/decisions/`.

Part of #1907

body:
**The request (mkinney, 2026-11-15):** "Can we have better docs on how to do 3+1 and continuous 4 axis milling? ... I want to use my microArc4." The user has a Tormach 770MX with a microARC 4 (machine file `assets/machines/tormach-770mx-microarc4.mch`).

Today the pages are short: `multi-axis/indexed.md` (101 lines), `continuous-4-axis.md` (74 lines) and `machines-and-tcp.md` (83 lines). They name the microARC 4 only once or twice. There is no complete worked example.

Wanted: two step-by-step walkthroughs on the 770MX + microARC 4, each with a small committed demo project and images (see the example-images issue):
1. **Indexed 3+1:** a part with features on several faces (for example a hex or a square bar with holes and pockets on four sides).
   - Mount the part between centres or in a chuck on the A axis. Set the work offset on the rotary centreline (how to find it and probe it).
   - Make one setup per index angle, or one setup with indexed operations. The guide says which one CamCraft prefers and why.
   - How the post writes the A moves (unwind, clamp/unclamp if any, safe retract before an index).
   - The checks: collision with the rotary and tailstock, and reach.
2. **Continuous 4-axis:** wrapping (an engraving or a slot wrapped on a cylinder) and a rotary roughing or finishing pass.
   - The operation choices, the feed-rate mode (inverse time or degrees per minute, and what the 770MX post writes), and the A-axis feed cap.
   - Simulation and verify for 4-axis, and what a refusal means here.
3. **Machine setup:** the microARC 4 machine file fields (A axis direction, limits, max rpm and feed), and the PathPilot settings to check before the first run.
4. **Prove it out:** a dry run in the PathPilot Hub 770MX simulator with the 4th axis enabled. Which numbers to check: the A-axis direction and the wrap scale.

Clean room: CamCraft behaviour, Tormach's public documentation and general machining knowledge only.

body:
Maintainer request from #1572 ("make an issue of using cadmpeg as file importer then i suppose.. we could open all common cad parts into camcraft that way.").

## Goal
Run `cadmpeg` as an optional external CLI process from `camcraft-app` to convert native CAD files into STEP inside a strict sandbox, then import through the existing STEP pipeline.

## Scope
- Add an optional `cadmpeg_path: Option<String>` field to `ViewPrefs` in `crates/app/src/prefs.rs` (`camcraft-prefs/1`) so existing `prefs.json` files still load cleanly.
- Resolve the executable cleanly on desktop (`cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))`): check `cadmpeg_path` first if set, then search `PATH`. Return `CommandError::Needs` naming `cadmpeg` and the file extension when missing.
- Probe `cadmpeg --version` and enforce minimum version `0.6.12`. Probe `cadmpeg formats --json` to confirm STEP export and codec availability. Report old or unusable binaries via named `CommandError` variants (`CommandError::Needs` / `CommandError::Invalid`).
- Pass file paths directly through `std::process::Command::new` argv with no shell invocation.
- Run conversions inside a unique private directory under `std::env::temp_dir()` owned by an RAII `Drop` guard that removes the directory on success, error, or panic.
- Enforce a child execution timeout (kill on expiry), bounded stdout/stderr buffers, and `MAX_FILE_BYTES` output size limit (`crates/app/src/geometry/import/mod.rs`).
- Execute `cadmpeg check --json <input>` and `cadmpeg convert <input> -o <step_out> --to step --reject-lossy=export` without `--allow-errors`. Refuse nonzero exits, blocking findings, or empty outputs by name.
- Pass converted STEP output into `crates/app/src/geometry/import/step.rs` (`step::parse_open`) and all existing STEP guards (`step_depth`, `step_edge3d`, `step_closed::closed_shells`, `step_guard`, `step_refine`, `step_outward`).
- Replace the hardcoded `"iges" | "igs"` `CommandError::UnsupportedType` arm in `ImportModel::checked_budget` (`crates/app/src/commands/import_model.rs`) with routing through the shared qualified-extension table. Keep the table empty until format qualification enables passing formats, and refuse unqualified extensions such as `L1` `.prt` by name.
- Add desktop unit tests using stub executables for success, missing binary, old version, nonzero `cadmpeg check`, timeout cleanup, oversized STEP refusal, and garbage output without touching `Cargo.toml` dependencies.

## Done means
`camcraft-app` resolves `cadmpeg`, enforces version `>= 0.6.12`, converts in a cleaned temp dir with timeout and size caps, refuses `check` errors by name, feeds output into `step::parse_open`, and passes stub-binary tests without new `Cargo.toml` crates.

title: Circular (ramp entry): stay at depth between levels instead of retracting to the clearance height and rapiding back to the cut floor

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P7
labels.description: Owed polish and small fixes

body:
What happens: a Circular operation with entry Ramp (helical, after PR #1663) retracts to the clearance height after every depth level, then rapids straight back down to the floor it just cut, then starts the next helix. Seen in a PathPilot Hub run on the 770MX simulator, 2026-11-14 (file `hub-tests/1663-circular-ramp/pr.nc`, PR head 8d63209a; T4 4 mm end mill; 6 mm hole, two rings r 0.0394 and r 0.0197; steps 0.0394 in):

```
G3 X-1.3386 Y0.1142 Z-0.0987 I0.0394 J0 F19.69   (last ring of the level)
G0 X-1.3386 Y0.1142 Z0.1969                       (rapid up to clearance)
G0 X-1.3386 Y0.1142 Z-0.0987                      (rapid down to the floor just cut)
G3 X-1.4066 Y0.1412 Z-0.1037 I-0.0394 J0 F19.69   (next helix starts)
```

It is safe: the moves are straight up and down at one X/Y inside the cut hole. But:
- Each level adds an air trip to the clearance height and back. That costs time on a deep hole with many levels.
- The rapid down ends exactly on the previous floor, with no gap. A rapid usually stops a small clearance above the floor, and the last part is fed.

Wanted: between depth levels of one Circular operation, either
- (a) stay at depth: the next helix continues from the end of the last ring with no retract (the material below is uncut, and the helix ramps into it), or
- (b) if a retract is kept, rapid down only to a small clearance above the previous floor (for example the operation's ramp clearance), then feed the rest.

(a) is preferred. A retract should stay only where the tool must leave the hole (the last level, or a level change that needs a lift). The ramp entry and the refusals stay unchanged. The posted G-code changes, so update the circular goldens with the reason.

Found while running the Hub check for PR #1663 (issue #1609).

Done means: a pin shows no rapid to the clearance height between levels of one Circular operation (or, with option b, no rapid that ends below the previous floor plus the clearance). The circular goldens are updated, and the stock simulation still shows no gouge.

Change: add an operation parameter `gap_link` to the finishing parameters. The parameter is a dropdown with two options:

- `Jump` (default): today's behaviour, unchanged. The chain lifts to the retract plane.
- `Straight`: one straight Feed move between the end of one run and the start of the next, at the two end points' own tip height.

Law for `Straight`: both run ends stand at tangent centers by the march construction. The author certifies the exact segment-triangle sweep of the move at the budget `r - TOUCH_EPS`. A grazing contact at the rim passes. A real bite refuses. On a refusal the chain takes the `Jump` hop. No air margin is added for `Straight`; `Jump` keeps its own retract law.

Also fixed, needed by this feature: the raster serpentine ran a broken back line wrong. It reversed only each piece's points and kept the pieces in grid order. Every gap link then jumped back across the field instead of crossing its gap. A back line now reverses whole: the pieces in reverse order, and each piece's points reversed. This also shortens the existing `Jump` traverses on broken lines.

How the parameter is stored: the project digest takes a `0x4D` tag plus a variant byte only when `gap_link` is not `Jump`. The project file grammar takes the words `jump` and `straight`. No project-file version step-up. The MCP params door and the UI combo carry the same two options.

Done means:

- The Gap link dropdown offers Jump and Straight; Jump is the default and writes the old bytes.
- Over a holed plate, `Straight` authors rim-to-rim Feed links at the run height and no retract hop for those gaps.
- A `Straight` link that would cut the part is refused, and the hop stands (Prime Directive).
- Every gap crossing on a broken back line spans one gap, never the field.
- Pins: `crates/motion/tests/finish3d_gaplink.rs`, the round-trip pins in `crates/app/tests/project_roundtrip.rs`, and the MCP params-door test.
