labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
What happens: `assets/posts/tormach-lathe.cps` (`g76Grid`) takes J (first depth) to the grid with `floor` and K from the rounded peak and outward-rounded root, each on its own. LinuxCNC's `R1` (constant depth) ladder cuts J, 2J, ... clamped at K, so it cuts ceil(K/J) passes. The inch golden `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach-lathe/thread_g76_inch.nc` posts `G76 P0.07874 Z0.315 I-0.004 J0.0314 K0.0944 R1 Q0 H0`: 0.0944 / 0.0314 = 3.006, so the control cuts 0.0314, 0.0628, 0.0942 and a 0.0944 pass (0.0002 in on diameter), 4 passes where the record laid and the verdict judged 3 (0.4 / 0.8 / 1.2 mm radius). The mm golden (`J0.8 K2.4`) is exact.

Not a gouge: the extra pass is shallower than the root and the root is rounded outward. But the posted words state a pass schedule that was not verified, the same class of mismatch #417 removes on the Fanuc lathe (PR #517 review, where the Fanuc inch R was fixed by deriving it from the rounded words' own ladder).

Expected: the grid words' own ladder cuts exactly the record's pass count: e.g. choose J (and K within the outward-root rule) so ceil(K/J) equals the record's rung count, or refuse by name when the grid cannot state it. Semantics from the LinuxCNC G76 documentation (R1 = constant depth, K = full depth).

Note: the inch golden was run on the PathPilot Hub 8L sim to M30 with no alarm (PR #517 comments); that run does not check the pass count. A fix changes that golden and needs a new Hub run.

Found while fixing the M3 review of PR #517 (#417); left out of that PR because its Tormach goldens must stay byte-identical to main.

Done means: the Tormach inch G76 words make LinuxCNC's ladder cut exactly the record's passes (a test parses the posted J/K and counts ceil(K/J) against the record), or the record is refused by name; mm output unchanged.

title: post-merge.yml: the report job is skipped when the gate fails, so a red main opens no issue

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:low
labels.description: Mechanical, one file, no new logic (issue-worker-low)

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
What happens: post-merge run 43535610115 (push to main at 745edc36a) ended with job `gate` = failure and job `report` = skipped. The rolling issue `main is red (post-merge gate)` was not opened or commented on.

Expected: AGENTS.md "Fixes are tested in the background": a red post-merge gate opens or comments on the rolling issue; the next green run closes it.

Cause (read from `.github/workflows/post-merge.yml` on main): the `report` job has `needs: gate` and an `if:` with no status-check function:

```
if: ${{ (needs.gate.result == 'success' || needs.gate.result == 'failure') && needs.gate.outputs.skipped != 'true' && (...) }}
```

GitHub Actions adds an implicit `success()` to a job's `if` unless it contains `always()`, `failure()`, `cancelled()` or `!cancelled()`. With a failed `needs` job the implicit `success()` is false, so the job is skipped before the expression is read. The job therefore only ever runs on green.

Suggested fix: start the condition with `always() &&` (the rest already excludes cancelled and skipped runs). One line.

Note on this particular run: its only red test was `a_lowered_cap_refuses_the_same_face_at_once` (`crates/app/tests/import_step_guard.rs`, "not within 30s"), the wall-clock flake of issue 1605, so main was not truly red here. The reporting gap is real for any failure.

A `.github/` change: the PR is read, not built, and waits for the maintainer (`needs-maintainer`). `Process change: yes` does not apply (`.github/` is not a process file).

Found by the maintenance session while watching runs.

Done means: a post-merge run whose gate fails runs `report` and opens or comments on the rolling issue; a green run after it closes that issue; a cancelled or cut-skipped run still reports nothing.

Part of #1445.

The first slice of #1445 (the ream, G85) left fine boring out on purpose. A fine-boring cycle stops the spindle at a fixed orientation at the bottom, shifts the tip away from the wall, then rapids out. The shift direction and amount depend on how the boring bar is clamped relative to the spindle's orientation angle. A guessed default could drag the tip across the finished bore, so no default is posted.

What is owed:
- A drill-op cycle choice for fine boring, with two required user parameters: the shift direction (or angle) and the shift amount, validated at command creation (finite, positive amount, smaller than the hole radius minus the tool's tip extent).
- A machine capability for oriented spindle stop; a machine or post without it refuses the cycle by name, never posts a plain bore in its place.
- Posts that have the canned word write it, with the shift words in that control's own form; the others refuse by name (an expanded chain needs M19-style orientation, which is per control).
- The CL chain the verifier and simulation read: feed in, (dwell), shift, rapid out, so the rapid out is judged against the wall at the shifted position.
- MCP `edit_operation` parameters for both values, a UI row in plain English.

Sources: public controller documentation only (RS-274/NGC, LinuxCNC; vendor programming manuals for the word layout). RS-274/NGC uses G76 for lathe threading; the fine-boring word differs by control and must be read from each post, not assumed.

Done means: fine boring is a user choice that posts only with an orientation-capable machine and an explicit shift, is refused by name otherwise, and is pinned by per-post goldens and a verifier test of the shifted retract.

**How it must fit the laws**
- Everything Is a Command: a drag is a PREVIEW while the mouse is down (ephemeral, immediate-mode) and ONE undoable command on release - the same model-transform command the Model page's position/rotation fields queue, never a field poke. Escape during a drag cancels with no history step; a zero-length drag adds none.
- Moving a body changes where the part sits: operations generated before the move must read as stale (as they do when the fields are edited); anything derived from the model's placement (the stock "from model", the raw-stock-only mark of #1094 that is void after a move, fixtures located on the part) behaves exactly as with a typed-in move. No new placement path.
- What may be dragged: models, and (decide, with the reason) fixtures and the stock. The work origin already has its own page; do not move it with this gizmo unless the maintainer says so.
- Picking a ball must not fight orbit/pan: a ball under the cursor wins, empty space still orbits. Handles keep a constant size on screen. Snapping (to a grid step, to 90 degrees for rotate) with a modifier key is a parameter with a default, shown in the bar.
- The number is still there: while dragging, the bar shows the distance or angle, and typing a value applies it exactly (same command).
- Layering ui -> app; MCP already moves a model through the transform command - if a new command is added it gets its MCP tool.
- Pixel goldens of the viewport differ at the next cut; pin the behaviour in structural / interaction tests (handles present for a selected body, a drag queues exactly one transform command with the dragged distance, Escape queues none, the overlay holds the buttons that used to be on the right).

**Slices** (each its own PR with `Refs` until the last): (a) the bottom overlay bar with the existing right-hand buttons moved into it; (b) move handles with drag-to-move; (c) rotate; (d) snapping and typed values in the bar.

Done means: a body can be moved and rotated by dragging its gizmo handles, each drag is one undo step, the Move/Rotate choice and the former right-edge buttons live in a rounded grey overlay bar at the bottom of the viewport, and nothing about placement can be changed that the Model page's fields could not change.

body:
PR #888 (`Fixes #887`) pins `ruststep` and `ruststep-derive` to an unreleased upstream commit through `[patch.crates-io]` in the root `Cargo.toml` - the workspace's only git dependency. The maintainer accepted it on 2026-11-11 "for now, but drop it as soon as upstream is released".

Blocked on: a crates.io release of `ruststep` newer than 0.4.0 that contains the empty parameter list fix (upstream ricosjp/ruststep; its issue #256 asks for the release).

When it is out: set `ruststep = "=<new version>"`, remove the `[patch.crates-io]` entries and their comment, let `Cargo.lock` return to the registry source with checksums, and run `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test import` plus the STEP suites.

Why it matters: a git dependency is only as available as the upstream repo, and audit tools read the lock's version (0.4.0) for code that is not 0.4.0.

Done means: no `[patch.crates-io]` entry and no `git+` source for ruststep in `Cargo.lock`; the #887 fixture still imports.

Depends on PR #888 merging first.

title: Process changes - fork maintainers please subscribe

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: P?
labels.description: Paused: never picked until the maintainer sets a real priority

body:
**Subscribe to this issue** (the "Subscribe" button on the right) if you work from a fork of CamCraft, especially with an AI agent.

Forks sync product code only at release tags (AGENTS.md "A fork syncs from upstream at each cut tag"). But the *process* - `AGENTS.md`, the agent definitions in `.claude/agents/`, the skills in `.claude/skills/` and `scripts/gate.*` - changes between releases, and a fork's agents should follow the current rules (review labels, priority labels, release steps, and so on).

**How it works:**
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` holds one number. Every PR that changes a process file bumps it.
- Every such PR also adds a comment **here**: the new version, what changed, and what to pull. Subscribers get one notification per change.
- A fork's agent compares its `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` with upstream's at the start of each session and, if upstream is newer, pulls just the process files (AGENTS.md "Process files sync on every session"). Product code still waits for the next release tag.

**To pull by hand:**
```
git fetch upstream
git checkout upstream/main -- AGENTS.md .claude/agents .claude/skills .claude/PROCESS_VERSION scripts/gate.ps1 scripts/gate.sh
git commit -m "chore(process): sync process files to upstream PROCESS_VERSION <n>"
```

This issue stays open and pinned. It's labelled `P?` so no agent ever picks it up as work.
